FORM 27. (\forall \alpha )(UT(\aleph _{0}, \aleph _{\alpha }, \aleph _{\alpha })): The union of denumerably many sets each of power \aleph _{\alpha } has power \aleph _{\alpha }. G. Moore [1982] p 36.
FORM 28. C(\aleph _{0},2^{\aleph _{0}}): Every denumerable collection of non-empty sets each with power 2^{\aleph _{0}} has a choice function. Sierpiński [1918].

FORM 29. If |S|=\aleph _{0} and \{A_{x}:x\in S\} and \{B_{x}:x\in S\} are families of pairwise disjoint sets and |A_{x}|=|B_{x}| for all x\in S, then |\bigcup _{x\in S}A_{x}|=|\bigcup _{x\in S}B_{x}|. G. Moore [1982] p 324.
FORM 30. Ordering Principle: Every set can be linearly ordered. Schröder [1988].
[30 A] If R is a partial ordering in which the set of predecessors of each element is linearly ordered, then there is a linear ordering extending R. Felgner [1969].

[30 B] ADO: Every infinite set differs finitely from a set with a dense linear ordering: for all infinite x, there is a y\subseteq x such that y has a dense linear ordering and x-y is finite. Pincus [1997].
[30 C] SADO: For every set F there is a function f with domain F such that for all x\in F,\, f(x)\subseteq x,\,f(x) has a dense linear ordering, and x-f(x) is finite. Pincus [1997].
[30 D] UO: There exists an unbounded linear ordering on every infinite set. (An ordering is unbounded if there is neither a least element nor a greatest element.) Pincus [1997].
[30 E] ADUO: For all infinite x, there exists y\subseteq x such that y has a dense unbounded linear ordering and x-y is finite. Pincus [1997].
[30 F] SADUO: For every set F there is a function f with domain F such that for all x\in F,\, f(x)\subseteq x,\,f(x) has a dense unbounded linear ordering, and x-f(x) is finite. Pincus [1997].
[30 G] Weak Hausdorff Lemma: For every set X, every \subseteq -chain in \mathcal{P}(X) is contained in a maximal \subseteq -chain. Note 130.
FORM 31. UT(\aleph _{0}, \aleph _{0}, \aleph _{0}): The countable union theorem: The union of a denumerable set of denumerable sets is denumerable. Cantor [1878].
FORM 32. C(\aleph _{0}, \leq \aleph _{0}): Every denumerable set of non-empty countable sets has a choice function. Sierpiński [1918].
[32 A] C(\aleph _{0}, \aleph _{0}). Every denumerable set of denumerable sets has a choice function.
[32 B] PC(\aleph _{0}, \aleph _{0}, \infty ): Every denumerable set of denumerable sets has an infinite subset with a choice function.
[32 C] PC(WO, \aleph _{0}, \infty ): Every infinite well ordered set of denumerable sets has an infinite subset with a choice function.
FORM 33(n). If n\in \omega -\{0,1\},\,C(LO, n): Every linearly ordered set of n element sets has a choice function. Truss [1973a].
FORM 34. \aleph _{1} is regular. Russell [1906] and note 3.
[34 A] \exists \alpha < \omega _{2} such that there are no hereditarily countable sets of rank \alpha . Jech [1982] and note 48.
[34 B] \omega _{1} with the order topology is not paracompact. Good/Tree [1995] and note 107.
[34 C] \omega _{1} with the order topology has the property that every infinite subset has a limit point in \omega _{1}. Good/Tree [1995] and note 107.
[34 D] \omega _{1} with the order topology does not contain a countable discrete family of open subsets. Good/Tree [1995] and note 107.
[34 E] \omega _{1} with the order topology is not Lindelöf. Good/Tree [1995] and note 107.
FORM 35. The union of countably many meager subsets of \mathbb{R} is meager. (Meager sets are the same as sets of the first category.) Feferman/Levy [1963], Jech [1973b] p 7 prob 1.7, and note 28.
FORM 36. If A\subseteq \mathbb{R}^{n} and A \bigcap B is countable for every bounded B then A is countable. G. Moore [1982] p 36.
FORM 37. Lebesgue measure is countably additive. Sierpiński [1916].
FORM 38. \mathbb{R} is not the union of a countable family of countable sets. Feferman/Levy [1963] and note 3.
[38 A] UT(\aleph _{0}, \aleph _{0}, \neq 2^{\aleph _{0}}): A denumerable union of denumerable sets does not have cardinality 2^{\aleph _{0}}.
FORM 39. C(\aleph _{1}, \infty ): Every set A of non-empty sets such that |A|=\aleph _{1} has a choice function. Sierpiński [1918], G. Moore [1982] p. 202.
FORM 40. C(WO, \infty ): Every well orderable set of non-empty sets has a choice function. G. Moore [1982] p 325.
[40 A] A(L2, L1): For every T_{2} topological space (X, T), if each open cover of X has a well ordered subcover, then each open cover has a well ordered refinement. Brunner [1983a] and note 26.

[40 B] For all ordinals \alpha , the \aleph _{\alpha } partition principle holds: For every ordinal \alpha and every cardinal \kappa , if \aleph _{\alpha }\leq ^{\ast }\kappa , then \aleph _{\alpha }\leq \kappa . Pelc [1978], Banaschewski/Moore [1990], and note 69.

[40 C] For each idemmultiple set x\ (2\times x\approx x), if there exists a surjection f mapping x onto an ordinal \lambda such that for each \psi <\lambda ,\,f^{-1}[\{\psi \}] is Dedekind infinite, then \lambda \precsim x. Higasikawa [1995] and note 94.
FORM 41. W_{\aleph _{1}}: For every cardinal m,\,m\leq \aleph _{1} or \aleph _{1}\leq m. Jech [1973b].
FORM 42. Löwenheim-Skolem Theorem: If a countable family of first order sentences is satisfiable in a set M then it is satisfiable in a countable subset of M. G. Moore [1982] p 251.

FORM 43. DC(\omega ) (DC), Principle of Dependent Choices: If S is a relation on a non-empty set A and (\forall x\in A)(\exists y\in A)(xSy) then there is a sequence a(0),a(1),a(2),\ldots of elements of A such that (\forall n\in \omega ) (a(n)\,S\,a(n+1)). Tarski [1948] p 96 , Levy [1964] p 136 and note 54.

[43 A] Tarski’s Lemma: Let \{x(n) : n\in \omega \} be a denumerable collection of subsets of a Boolean algebra B each of which has a meet in B. Then for any a\neq 0 in B there is a proper filter F of B that decides \bigwedge x(n) for all n and has a\in F. (F decides \bigwedge x(n) if either \bigwedge x(n)\in F or t\not \in F for some t\in x(n).) Goldblatt [1985].

[43 B] Countable Henkin Principle: Let \Phi be the class of formulas in a language that includes the language of the sentential calculus. Let I be a countable set of inferences, and \Gamma a consistent subset of \Phi such that \Gamma \cup \{\psi \} respects I for each \psi \in \Phi . Then for any \phi \in \Phi , if \phi is consistent with \Gamma then \Gamma has a finitely consistent extension that contains \phi and decides I. Goldblatt [1985] and note.

[43 C] Existence of a generic set: If \mathcal{D} is a denumerable collection of dense sets in a partial order (P, \leq ) then for all p\in P there is a \mathcal{D} generic G with p\in G. Goldblatt [1985] and note 47.

[43 D] If \mathcal{D} is a denumerable collection of dense subsets of a partial order (P, \leq ) then for all p\in P there is a sequence f:\omega \rightarrow P with f(0)=p and (\forall n\in \omega )(f(n)\geq f(n+1)) and range (f) \cap D\neq \emptyset for all D\in \mathcal{D}. Goldblatt [1985].
[43 E] The Baire Category Theorem for Čech Complete-I Spaces: Every Čech complete space is Baire. Goldblatt [1985] and note 28.
[43 F] Baire Category Theorem for Sequentially Complete Metric Spaces: Every sequentially complete metric space is Baire. Blair [1977], Brunner [1983b], Goldblatt [1985], and note 28.
[43 G] Form 106 + form 154. Brunner [1983b] [1984b].
[43 H] Every tree in which every element has at least one successor has a branch. Blass [1979] and note note 21.
[43 I] Form [106 A] + form 10. Blass [1979].
[43 J] Baire Category Theorem for Cantor Complete Metric Spaces: Every Cantor complete metric space is Baire. Brunner [1983b] and note 28.
[43 K] Let M be a non-empty set partially ordered by < without <-minimal elements. Then there is a subset C of M which is linearly ordered by < such that C has no <-minimal element. Note 146.
[43 L] Z_{\omega }: If every chain in a partially ordered set P is finite, then P contains a maximal element. Tarski [1948], Wolk [1983], and note 54.

[43 M] If (X, \rho ) is a complete metric space and \phi :X\rightarrow \mathbb{R} is bounded above and upper semi-continuous then in the Brøndsted ordering, (x\leq y iff \rho (x, y)\leq \phi (y)-\phi (x)), there is a maximal element. Brunner [1987a] and note 38.

[43 N] RM1,\,\aleph _{0}: The representation theorem for multi-algebras with \aleph _{0} unary operations: Assume (A, F) is a multi-algebra with \aleph _{0} unary operations (and no other operations), then there is an algebra (B, G) with \aleph _{0} unary operations and an equivalence relation E on B such that (B/E, G/E) and (A, F) are isomorphic multi-algebras. Note 50 and Höft/Howard [1981].

[43 O] (Depends on n\in \omega ,\ n\geq 1)\ RM1,\,n: The representation theorem for multi-algebras with n unary operations: Assume (A, F) is a multi-algebra with n unary operations (and no other operations), then there is an algebra (B, G) with n unary operations and an equivalence relation E on B such that (B/E, G/E) and (A, F) are isomorphic multi-algebras. Höft/Howard [1981] and note 50.
[43 P] The ultraproduct of a well founded structure by a countably complete ultrafilter is well founded. Spector [1980] and note 54.

[43 Q] Matrix(\omega ): For every atomless poset (P, \leq ) and every family D=\{D_{i}:i\in \omega \} of dense open subsets of P, there exists a matrix C=\{C_{i}:i\in \omega \},\, |\bigcup C|=\omega of P for D. Keremedis [1996] and note 132.

[43 R] Any partial order (A, \leq ) with no infinite descending chains is well founded, (that is, for all X such that \emptyset \neq X\subseteq A, X has a minimal element.) Spector [1980] and note 54.

[43 S] If S is a relation on A such that (\forall x\in A)(\exists y\in A)(x\,S\, y) and x_{0} is any element of A, then there is a sequence a(1),a(2),\ldots of elements of A such that a(n)\,S\,a(n+1) for all n\in \omega and such that a(0)=x_{0}. Notes 101 and 54.
[43 T] A sequentially complete metric space is not meager. Note 28.
[43 U] Baire Category Theorem for Filter Complete Metric Spaces: Every filter complete metric space is Baire, Morillon [1988] and note 28.
[43 V] Every convex-compact set in a Hausdorff topological vector space with a basis of convex open sets is Baire. Fossy/Morillon [1995] and note 23.

FORM 44. DC(\aleph _{1}): Given a relation R such that for every subset Y of a set X with |Y|<\aleph _{1} there is an x\in X with Y\ R\,x, then there is a function f:\aleph _{1}\rightarrow X such that (\forall \beta <\aleph _{1})(\{f(\gamma ):\gamma <b\}\,R\,f(\beta )). Levy [1964].
FORM 45(n). If n\in \omega -\{0,1\},\,C(\infty , n): Every set of n-element sets has a choice function. Mostowski [1945], Truss [1973a].
FORM 46(K). If K is a finite subset of \omega -\{0,1\},\,C(\infty , K): For every n\in K, every set of n-element sets has a choice function. Mostowski [1945], Truss [1973a].
FORM 47(n). If n\in \omega -\{0, 1\},\,C(WO, n): Every well ordered collection of n-element sets has a choice function. Mostowski [1945], Truss [1973a].
FORM 48(K). If K is a finite subset of \omega -\{0, 1\},\,C(WO, K): For every n\in K,\,C(WO, n). Mostowski [1945], Truss [1973a].
FORM 49. Order Extension Principle: Every partial ordering can be extended to a linear ordering. Tarski [1924] p 78.

FORM 50. Sikorski’s Extension Theorem: Every homomorphism of a subalgebra B of a Boolean algebra A into a complete Boolean algebra B^{\prime } can be extended to a homomorphism of A into B^{\prime }. Sikorski [1964], p 141.
[50 A] Every complete Boolean algebra is injective. Banaschewski [1988].

[50 B] Monteiro’s Theorem: Let K be a complete Boolean algebra, A a subalgebra of the Boolean algebra B and f a homomorphism from A to K. Let d be a semimorphism from B into K (that is, d:B\rightarrow K, d(0)=0,\,d(1)=1 and for all x and y in B,\,d(x\vee y)=d(x)\vee d(y)) with f(x)\leq d(x) for all x\in A. Then there is a homomorphism h from B to K such that h(x)\leq d(x) for all x\in B and h/A=f. Monteiro [1965] and Bacsich [1972a].
[50 C] Every DeMorgan compact regular frame is injective in the category of all such frames. Banaschewski [1988], notes 29 and 60.

[50 D] For any extension M\supseteq L of a compact regular frame L, there is an s\in M maximal with respect to the property that x\vee s=1\rightarrow x=1 for all x\in L. Banaschewski [1988], notes 29 and 60.
[50 E] Form 14 + form 297. Banaschewski [1988] and Bell [1988].

[50 F] For any complete Boolean algebra B and any subalgebra A of B, there is a U\in V^{(B)} such that V^{(B)}\models ``U is an ultrafilter on A and U^{B}\subseteq U\mbox{''}. (V^{(B)} is the Boolean valued universe constructed from B,\,U^{B}=\{(\hat{x}, x):x\in B\} is the canonical ultrafilter on B and x\mapsto \hat{x} is the canonical embedding of V into V^{(B)}.) Bell [1977] and [1983].

[50 G] For any complete Boolean algebra B and any C\in V^{(B)} such that V^{(B)}\models ``C is a Boolean algebra.” there is a U\in V^{(B)} such that V^{(B)}\models ``U is an ultrafilter in C.” See [50 F] for definitions. Bell [1983].

[50 H] If m:A\rightarrow B is a monomorphism between Boolean algebras, then there is an m-minimal epimorphism p:B\rightarrow C to some Boolean algebra C. (p is m-minimal if (1) p\circ m is monic and (2) if q:C\rightarrow D is any epimorphism to a Boolean algebra D such that q\circ p\circ m is monic, then q is an isomorphism.) Bell [1988].
[50 I] If A is a subalgebra of a Boolean algebra B, then there is a \subseteq -maximal proper filter F in B such that F\cap A=\{1\}. Bell [1988]
[50 J] Form 299 + form 14. Bell [1988].
[50 K] Form 300 + form 14. Bell [1988].
[50 L] Form 301 + form 14. Bell [1988].
[50 M] Form 302 + form 14. Bell [1988].
FORM 51. Cofinality Principle: Every linear ordering has a cofinal sub well ordering. Sierpiński [1918] p 117.
[51 A] For all linear orders (X, \leq ), there is a \displaystyle \sup function on the bounded, well ordered subsets of X. Manka [1988] and note 38.

[51 B] Z(L, W): Every non-empty linearly ordered set in which every well ordered subset has an upper bound has a maximal element. Harper/Rubin [1976], Manka [1988], H. Rubin/J. Rubin [1985] p 37 M1(L, W), and note 39.
[51 C] For every linearly ordered set (X, \leq ), if every well ordered subset of X is bounded above then there is a sup function on the well ordered subsets of X. Manka [1988] and note 38.

FORM 52. Hahn-Banach Theorem: If V is a real vector space and p:V\rightarrow \mathbb{R} satisfies p(x+y)\leq p(x)+p(y) and (\forall t>0)(p(tx)=tp(x)) and S is a subspace of V and f:S\rightarrow \mathbb{R} is linear and satisfies (\forall x\in S)(f(x)\leq p(x)) then f can be extended to f^{\ast }:V\rightarrow \mathbb{R} such that f^{\ast } is linear and (\forall x\in V)(f^{\ast }(x)\leq p(x)). Lós/Ryll-Nardzewski [1951].
[52 A] On every Boolean algebra there is an additive real valued measure. Luxemburg [1969] and note 147.

[52 B] For every proper filter \mathcal{F} of elements of a Boolean algebra \mathcal{B}, there exists an additive, real valued measure m on \mathcal{B} such that m(x)=1 for all x\in \mathcal{F}. Luxemburg [1969] and note 147.

[52 C] For every non-empty set X and every proper ideal \mathcal{I} of in \mathcal{P}(X) there is a measure m on \mathcal{P}(X) such that m(x)=0 for all x\in \mathcal{I}. Luxemburg [1969] and note 147.

[52 D] Let \mathcal{B}_{0} be a subalgebra of a Boolean algebra \mathcal{B} and m_{0} an additive, real valued measure on \mathcal{B}_{0}. Then there is a real valued, additive measure m on \mathcal{B} such that m=m_{0} on \mathcal{B}_{0} and the range of m is contained in the closed convex hull of the range of m_{0}. Luxemburg [1969] and note 147.
[52 E] The unit ball is convex-compact in the weak^\ast topology in the dual of a Banach space. (See [14 Q].) Luxemburg [1969], H. Rubin/J. Rubin [1985] p 178, and note 23.
[52 F] If X is a topological vector space then for every continuous sublinear functional p on E there is a linear functional f on E such that f\leq p. Fossy/Morillon [1995].
[52 G] If X is a normed vector space then for every continuous sublinear functional p on E there is a linear functional f on E such that f\leq p. Fossy/Morillon [1995].
[52 H] Existence of Real Valued Banach Limits: For any directed set (\Delta , \sqsubseteq ) there exists a (real valued) Banach limit. Schechter [1996b] and note 31.

[52 I] Real Valued Convex Domination Theorem: For every real vector space X, every subspace X_{0}\subseteq X, every linear \lambda _{0}:X_{0}\rightarrow \mathbb{R} and every convex p:X\rightarrow \mathbb{R}, if \lambda _{0}\leq p on X_{0} then \lambda _{0} can be extended to a linear map \lambda :X\rightarrow \mathbb{R} such that \lambda \leq p on X. Schechter [1996b] and note 31.

[52 J] Support Theorem for Real Valued Convex Functions: For every real vector space X, every convex function p:X\rightarrow \mathbb{R} is a pointwise maximum of affine functions. Schechter [1996b] and note 31.

[52 K] Sandwich Theorem for Real Valued Functions: For every real vector space X, if e:X\rightarrow \mathbb{R} is a concave function, g:X\rightarrow \mathbb{R} is a convex function, and e\leq g everywhere on X, then there exists an affine function f: X\rightarrow \mathbb{R} satisfying e\leq f\leq g everywhere on X. Schechter [1996b] and note 31.
FORM 53. For all infinite cardinals m,\,m^{2}\leq 2^{m}. Mathias [1979] prob 1336.
FORM 54. For all infinite cardinals m,\,m\ \mathrm{adj}\ 2^{m} implies m is an aleph. (m\ \mathit{adj}\ n iff m<n and (\neg \exists p)(m<p<n).) Mathias [1979] prob 1337, thm 1338 and prob 1339.
FORM 55. For all infinite cardinals m and n, if m\cdot n=m+n then, m\leq n or n\leq m. Mathias [1979] p 125.
FORM 56. \aleph (2^{\aleph _{0}})\neq \aleph _{\omega }. (\aleph (2^{\aleph _{0}}) is Hartogs’ aleph, the least \aleph not \leq 2^{\aleph _{0}}.) Mathias [1979] p 125.
FORM 57. If x and y are Dedekind finite sets then either |x|\leq |y| or |y|\leq |x|. Mathias [1979] p 125 and note 94.

FORM 58. There is an ordinal \alpha such that \aleph (2^{\aleph _{\alpha }})\neq \aleph _{\alpha +1}.\ (\aleph (2^{\aleph _{\alpha }}) is Hartogs’ aleph, the least \aleph not \leq 2^{\aleph _{\alpha }}.) Mathias [1979] p 126.

FORM 59(\leq ). If (A, \leq ) is a partial ordering that is not a well ordering, then there is no set B such that (B, \leq ) (the usual injective cardinal ordering on B) is isomorphic to (A, \leq ). Mathias [1979] p 120.
FORM 60. C(\infty , WO): Every set of non-empty, well orderable sets has a choice function. Jech [1973b], G. Moore [1982] p 125.
[60 A] (\forall \alpha )C(\infty , \aleph _{\alpha }): For every ordinal \alpha , every family of sets each with power \aleph _{\alpha } has a choice function.
FORM 61. (\forall n\in \omega , n\geq 2)(C(\infty , n)): For each n\in \omega , n\geq 2, every set of n element sets has a choice function. Levy [1962].
FORM 62. C(\infty , <\aleph _{0}): Every set of non-empty finite sets has a choice function.
[62 A] (Depends on the two primes p_{1}\neq p_{2}) Form 308(p_{1})\ + form 308(p_{2}). Howard/Yorke [1987].
[62 B] (Depends on the prime p_{1}) Form 45(p_{1})\ + form 308(p_{1}). Howard/Yorke [1987].
[62 C] For every prime p, if \{G_{y}:y\in Y\} is a set of finite groups, then the weak direct product \prod _{y\in Y}G_{y} has a maximal p-subgroup. Howard/Yorke [1987] and note 24.

[62 D] For every prime p, if Y is a set of non-empty, finite sets, then the weak direct product \prod _{y\in Y}S_{y} has a maximal p-subgroup. (S_{y} is the symmetric group on y.) Howard/Yorke [1987] and note 24.

[62 E] KW(\infty , <\aleph _{0}), The Kinna-Wagner Selection Principle for families of finite sets: For every set M of finite sets there is a function f such that for all A\in M, if |A|>1 then \emptyset \neq f(A)\subsetneq A. Note 70.
FORM 63. SPI: Weak ultrafilter principle: Every infinite set has a non-trivial ultrafilter. Jech [1973b] p 172 prob 8.5.
FORM 64. E(I, Ia) (Howard/Yorke [1989]): There are no amorphous sets. Note 94 and Levy [1958], notes 57 and 94.
[64 A] An amorphous power of a compact T_{2} space is compact. Brunner [1984b].
[64 B] Finite products of metric C spaces are C. (A space is C if each open covering has an amorphous refinement.) Brunner [1984b].
[64 C] C spaces are compact. (A space is a\ C space if each open covering has an amorphous refinement.) Brunner [1984b].

[64 D] Metric C spaces are limited amorphous. (A space is C if every open covering has an amorphous refinement. A space is limited amorphous if each amorphous subset is relatively compact.) Brunner [1984b].

FORM 65. The Krein-Milman Theorem: Let K be a compact convex set in a locally convex topological vector space X. Then K has an extreme point. (An extreme point is a point which is not an interior point of any line segment which lies in K.) Royden [1963] and H. Rubin/J. Rubin [1985], p. 177.
FORM 66. Every vector space over a field has a basis. Hamel [1905].

FORM 67. MC(\infty , \infty ) (MC), The Axiom of Multiple Choice: For every set M of non-empty sets there is a function f such that (\forall x\in M)(\emptyset \neq f(x)\subseteq x and f(x) is finite).

[67 A] A(A2, H2): For every T_{2} topological space (X, T) if (X, T) is A2, then (X, T) is hereditarily A2. ((X, T) is A2 means if U\subseteq T covers X then \exists f:X\rightarrow T such that for all x\in X,\,x\in f(x) and f” X refines U.) Brunner [1983a] and note 26.
[67 B] MW: Each set can be covered by a well ordered family of finite sets. Levy [1962].
[67 C] A(P): (Depends on P\in \{D1, B2, B3, H2, A2\}.) Every T_{2} topological space has property P. Brunner [1983a] and note 26.
[67 D] For every Abelian group A, every torsion free divisible subgroup of A is a direct summand of A. Armbrust [1972a] and note 24.

[67 E] For any algebra A with finitary operations (that is, A is of type \tau where \tau =(K_{i})_{i\in I} with K_{i} finite for each i\in I) and for any generating subset Z of A, there is a function h:A\rightarrow \mathcal{P}_{\omega }(Z) (A is the domain of A and \mathcal{P}_{\omega }(Z) is the set of all finite subsets of Z.) such that \forall a\in A,\ a is in the subalgebra of A generated by h(a). Diener [1989] and note 115.

[67 F] For any algebra A with one unary operation f and any generating set Z of A, there is a function h:A\rightarrow \mathcal{P}_{\omega }(Z) (A is the domain of A and \mathcal{P}_{\omega }(Z) is the set of all finite subsets of Z.) such that \forall a\in A,\,a is in the subalgebra of A generated by h(a). Diener [1989] and note 115.

[67 G] For every T_{1} topological space (X, T) and every cellular family \mathcal{O}= \{O_{i}:i\in k\}\subseteq T-\{\emptyset \}, there is a closed discrete set \mathcal{I} such that for every i\in k,\, \mathcal{I}\cap O_{i}\neq \emptyset . Keremedis [1996b] and note 77.

[67 H] Let (X, T) be a T_{4} topological space and let \{G_{i}:i\in K\} be a locally finite family of pairwise disjoint, non-empty, open subsets of X. Then there exists a continuous real valued function f:X\rightarrow \mathbb{R} such that for each i\in K,\,f vanishes on the boundary of G_{i} and f(x_{i})=1 for some x_{i}\in G_{i}. Keremedis [1995] and note 43.

[67 I] If (X, T) is a T_{4} topological space and U=\{U_{i}:i\in K\} is a family of non-empty open sets, then there is a family F=\{f_{i}:i\in K\} of non-negative, non-constant, continuous real valued functions on X such that each f_{i} vanishes on X-U_{i}. Keremedis [1995].

[67 J] If (X, T) is a T_{4} topological space and U=\{U_{i}:i\in K\} is a family of non-empty open sets, then there is a family V=\{V_{i}:i\in K\} of non-empty closed (compact) sets such that U_{i}\supseteq V_{i} for each i\in K. Keremedis [1995].
[67 K] DUN: The disjoint union of normal topological spaces is normal. Howard/Keremedis/Rubin/Rubin [1997a] and note 141.

[67 L] DUU: If C is a collection of pairwise disjoint topological spaces each of which satisfies Urysohn’s lemma, then the disjoint union of the spaces in C satisfies Urysohn’s lemma. Howard/Keremedis/Rubin/Rubin [1997a] and note 141.

[67 M] DUT: If C is a collection of pairwise disjoint topological spaces each of which satisfies the Tietze-Urysohn extension theorem, then the disjoint union of the spaces in C satisfies the Tietze-Urysohn extension theorem. Howard/Keremedis/Rubin/Rubin [1997a] and note 141.
[67 N] DUP: The disjoint union of paracompact spaces is paracompact. Howard/ Keremedis/Rubin/Rubin [1997b] and note 141.
[67 O] DUMET: The disjoint union of metacompact spaces is metacompact. Howard/Keremedis/Rubin/Rubin [1997b] and note 141.
[67 P] DUPFCS: The disjoint union of PFCS spaces is PFCS. (X is a PFCS space iff every point finite open cover of X is shrinkable.) Howard/Keremedis/ Rubin/Rubin [1997b] and note 141.
[67 Q] DUPN: The disjoint union of paracompact spaces is normal. Howard/ Keremedis/Rubin/Rubin [1997b] and note 141.
[67 R] DUcwH: The disjoint union of cwH spaces is cwH. Howard/Keremedis/ Rubin/Rubin [1997b] and note 141.
[67 S] DUcwN: The disjoint union of cwN spaces is cwN. Howard/Keremedis/ Rubin/Rubin [1997b] and note 141.
[67 T] DUcwNN: The disjoint union of cwN spaces is normal. Howard/Keremedis/Rubin/Rubin [1997b] and note 141.

[67 U] Every open cover \mathcal{U} of a metric space (X,\,d) can be written as a well ordered union \bigcup \{U_{\alpha }:\alpha \in \gamma \} where \gamma is an ordinal and each U_{\alpha } is locally finite. Howard/Keremedis/Rubin/Stanley [1997] and note 141.

[67 V] Every open cover \mathcal{U} of a metric space (X,\,d) can be written as a well ordered union \bigcup \{U_{\alpha }:\alpha \in \gamma \} where \gamma is an ordinal and each U_{\alpha } is point finite. Howard/Keremedis/Rubin/Stanley [1997] and note 141.
FORM 68. Nielsen-Schreier Theorem: Every subgroup of a free group is free. Jech [1973b] p 12.
FORM 69. Every field has an algebraic closure. Jech [1973b] p 13.
FORM 70. There is a non-trivial ultrafilter on \omega . Jech [1973b] prob 5.24.
[70 A] Every Dedekind infinite set has a non-principal ultrafilter.
[70 B] Weak Universal Net Theorem: There is a universal net in \omega which is not eventually constant. Schechter [1996a] and note 31.
[70 C] There is a 2-valued measure on \mathcal{P}(\omega ). Pincus [1972] and note 147.
FORM 71(\alpha ). W_{\aleph _{\alpha }}:(\forall x)(|x|\leq \aleph _{\alpha } or |x|\geq \aleph _{\alpha }). Pelc [1978], Jech [1973b], page 119 and Levy [1964].

FORM 72. Artin-Schreier Theorem: Every field in which -1 is not the sum of squares can be ordered. (The ordering, \leq , must satisfy (a) a\leq b\rightarrow a+c\leq b+c for all c and (b) c\geq 0 and a\leq b\rightarrow a\cdot c\leq b\cdot c.\rangle Tarski [1954b].
FORM 73. For every A\subseteq \mathbb{R} and x\in \mathbb{R} the following definitions are equivalent:
(1) x is in the closure of A iff every neighborhood of x intersects A.
(2) x is in the closure of A iff there is a sequence \{x_{n}\}\subseteq A such that \displaystyle \lim x_{n}=x. Jech [1973b] p 21.
[73 A] For all A\subseteq \mathbb{R},\,x\in A and f: A\rightarrow \mathbb{R} the following are equivalent:
(1) (\forall \epsilon >0)(\exists \delta >0)(\forall y\in A)(|y-x|<\delta implies |f(y)-f(x)|<\epsilon )
(2) Whenever \{x_{n}\}\subseteq A and \lim x_{n}=x then \lim f(x_{n})=f(x). Notes 4, 5 and 6.
[73 B] (\forall f:\mathbb{R} \rightarrow \mathbb{R})(\forall x\in \mathbb{R}) the following are equivalent:
(1) (\forall \epsilon >0)(\exists \delta >0)((\forall y\in \mathbb{R})(|y-x|<\delta \rightarrow |f(y)-f(x)|<\epsilon )
(2) Whenever \displaystyle \lim x_{n}=x, then \lim f(x_{n})=f(x). Note 10.
FORM 74. For every A\subseteq \mathbb{R} the following are equivalent:
(1) A is closed and bounded.
(2) Every sequence \{x_{n}\}\subseteq A has a convergent subsequence with limit in A. Jech [1973b] p 21.
FORM 75. Every subspace of a separable metric space is separable. Jech [1973b] p 21.

FORM 76. MC_{\omega }(\infty , \infty ) (\omega {-}\mathrm{MC}): For every family X of pairwise disjoint nonempty sets, there is a function f such that for each x\in X,\, \mathrm{f(x)} is a non-empty countable subset of x. Howard/Keremedis/Rubin/Rubin [1997b].

[76 A] Every open cover \mathcal{U} of a metric space can be written as a well ordered union \bigcup \{U_{\alpha }:\alpha \in \gamma \} where \gamma is an ordinal and each U_{\alpha } is locally countable. Howard/Keremedis/Rubin/Stanley [1997] and note 141.

[76 B] Every open cover \mathcal{U} of a metric space can be written as a well ordered union \bigcup \{U_{\alpha }:\alpha \in \gamma \} where \gamma is an ordinal and each U_{\alpha } is point countable. Howard/Keremedis/Rubin/Stanley [1997] and note 141.
FORM 77. A linear ordering of a set P is a well ordering if and only if P has no infinite descending sequences. Jech [1973b] p 23.
[77 A] If a linearly ordered set (X, \leq ) has no greatest element then it has a subset of order type \omega . Sierpiński [1918].

FORM 78. Urysohn’s Lemma: If A and B are disjoint closed sets in a normal space S, then there is a continuous f:S\rightarrow [0, 1] which is 1 everywhere in A and 0 everywhere in B. Urysohn [1925] pp 290-292.
FORM 79. \mathbb{R} can be well ordered. Hilbert [1900] p 263.
[79 A] C(\infty , \infty , \mathbb{R}): Every set whose elements are non-empty subsets of \mathbb{R} has a choice function. Schechter [1996a].
FORM 80. C(\aleph _{0},2): Every denumerable set of pairs has a choice function. Mostowski [1948].
[80 A] UT(\aleph _{0},2, \aleph _{0}): The union of denumerably many pairs is denumerable.

FORM 81(n). (For n\in \omega \ K(n): For every set S there is an ordinal \alpha and a one to one function f:S\rightarrow \mathcal{P}^{n}(\alpha ). (\mathcal{P}^{0}(X)=X and \mathcal{P}^{n+1}(X)=\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{P}^{n}(X)). (K(0) is equivalent to form 1 (AC) and K(1) is equivalent to the selection principle (form 15)). Monro [1972a], [1973b] and note 90.
FORM 82. E(I, III) (Howard/Yorke [1989]): If X is infinite then \mathcal{P}(X) is Dedekind infinite. (X is finite \Leftrightarrow \mathcal{P}(X) is Dedekind finite.) Levy [1958] and note 94.
[82 A]. Every infinite set can be mapped onto \omega . Howard/Yorke [1989], Monro [1972a].
[82 B] E(Ia, III): For every set X, if \mathcal{P}(X) is Dedekind finite then X is amorphous. Howard/Yorke [1989], notes 57 and 94.
FORM 83. E(I, II) (Howard/Yorke [1989]): T-finite is equivalent to finite. Tarski [1924] and note 94.
[83 A] E(Ia, II): Every T-finite set is amorphous. Howard/Yorke [1989], notes 57 and 94.
FORM 84. E(II, III) (Howard/Yorke [1989]): (\forall x)(x is T-finite if and only if \mathcal{P}(x) is Dedekind finite). Howard/Yorke [1989] and note 94.
FORM 85. C(\infty , \aleph _{0}): Every family of denumerable sets has a choice function. Jech [1973b] p 115 prob 7.13.
[85 A] C(\infty , \leq \aleph _{0}): Every family of non-empty countable sets has a choice function.
FORM 86(\alpha ). C(\aleph _{\alpha }, \infty ): If X is a set of non-empty sets such that |X|=\aleph _{\alpha }, then X has a choice function. Levy [1964].

[86 A(\alpha )] If (P, \leq ) is a tree of height \lambda \leq \aleph _{\alpha } which has fewer than \lambda branches of height <\lambda then one of the following holds for the upside down tree (P, \geq ):

def.p: There is a cardinal \mu <\lambda such that (P, \geq ) does not contain a strong antichain of cardinality \mu .
(P, \geq ) contains a strong antichain of cardinality \lambda .
(P, \geq ) contains a chain of cardinality \lambda .

sec.p: Shannon [1992] and note 119.
[86 B(\alpha )] The frame envelope of any \aleph _{\alpha } frame is \aleph _{\alpha }-Lindelöf. Banaschewski [1997] and note 29.

FORM 87(\alpha ). DC(\aleph _{\alpha }): Given a relation R such that for every subset Y of a set X with |Y|<\aleph _{\alpha }, there is an x\in X with Y\,R\,x then there is a function f:\aleph _{\alpha }\rightarrow X such that (\forall \beta <\aleph _{\alpha })\ \{f(\gamma ):\gamma <\beta \}\,R\,f(\beta ). Levy [1964].

[87 A(\alpha )] Z_{\aleph _{\alpha }}: Let P be a partially ordered set in which every well ordered chain has type <\aleph _{\alpha }. If every well ordered chain in P has an upper bound in P, then P contains a maximal element. Wolk [1983].

[87 B(\alpha )] Z_{\aleph _{\alpha }}^{\ast }: Let P be a well-founded partially ordered set (that is, every chain in P is well ordered.) in which every chain has type <\aleph _{\alpha }. If every chain in P has an upper bound in P, then P contains a maximal element. Wolk [1983].
FORM 88. C(\infty , 2): Every family of pairs has a choice function.

[88 A] P(2,2): If X is a set and P is a property of subsets of X of 2 character (that is, \forall y\subseteq X(P(y) iff \forall z\subseteq y(|z|\leq 2\rightarrow P(z)))) then if every finite subset of X can be partitioned into two or fewer P-sets (that is, sets z such that P(z)) then X can be partitioned into two or fewer P-sets. Cowen [1982].
[88 B] G_{2}: A graph is 2-colorable if every finite subgraph is 2-colorable. Mycielski [1961] and note 117.

[88 C] If m is a cardinal number and \mathcal{L} is a lattice isomorphic to the lattice of subalgebras of some unary universal algebra (a unary universal algebra is one with only unary or nullary operations) and \alpha is an automorphism of \mathcal{L} of order 2 (that is, \alpha ^{2} is the identity) then there is a unary algebra \mathfrak{A} with | domain \mathfrak{A}|\geq m and an isomorphism \rho from \mathcal{L} onto the lattice of subalgebras of \mathfrak{A}^{2} with \rho (\alpha (x))=(\rho (x))^{-1}(=\{(s, t):(t, s)\in \rho (x)\}) for all x\in \mathcal{L}. Lampe [1974].

[88 D] For any cardinal m, there is a unary algebra \mathfrak{A}=\langle A,\, F\rangle (only unary and nullary operations) and a proper subalgebra \mathfrak{D} of \mathfrak{A}^{2} such that \mathfrak{A}^{2} has exactly four subalgebras, \mathfrak{A},\,\emptyset ,\,\mathfrak{D} and \mathfrak{D}^{\ast }=\{(s, t):(t, s)\in \mathfrak{D}\}. Lampe [1974].
FORM 89. Antichain Principle: Every partially ordered set has a maximal antichain. Jech [1973b] p 133 and Kurepa [1953].

[89 A] If \forall y\in X,\,y=\langle u,\, R\rangle where R is a partial order on u then there is a function f on X such that \forall \langle u,\,R\rangle \in X,\,f(\langle u, R\rangle ) is a maximal antichain in u. Felgner [1969] and Harper/Rubin [1976].
FORM 90. LW: Every linearly ordered set can be well ordered. Jech [1973b] p 133 and Felgner/Jech [1973].
FORM 91. PW: The power set of a well ordered set can be well ordered. Jech [1973b] p 133 and H. Rubin/J. Rubin [1985].
[91 A] A(S, W1): For every T_{2} topological space (X,\, T) if X has a dense well ordered subset, then T is well ordered. (Clear) Brunner [1983a] and note 26.
FORM 92. Every subset of \mathbb{R} is separable. Jech [1973b] p 142.
FORM 93. There is a non-measurable subset of \mathbb{R}. Sierpiński [1918].
FORM 94. C(\aleph _{0}, \infty , \mathbb{R}): Every denumerable family of non-empty sets of reals has a choice function. Jech [1973b] p 148 prob 10.1.
[94 A] The discrete topology on \omega is Lindelöf. Brunner [1982d] and note 40.
[94B] There is a Lindelöf space with a closed, discrete infinite subset. Brunner [1982d] and note 40.

FORM 95 (F). Existence of Complementary Subspaces over a Field F: If F is a field, then every vector space V over F has the property that if S\subseteq V is a subspace of V, then there is a subspace S^{\prime }\subseteq V such that S\cap S^{\prime }=\{0\} and S\cup S^{\prime } generates V. Bleicher [1964], [1965], H. Rubin/J. Rubin [1985], pp 119ff, and Jech [1973b], p 148 prob 10.4.
FORM 96. Löwig’s Theorem. If B_{1} and B_{2} are both bases for the vector space V then |B_{1}|=|B_{2}|. Löwig [1934].

FORM 97. Cardinal Representatives: For every set A there is a function c with domain \mathcal{P}(A) such that for all x,\,y\in \mathcal{P}(A), (i) c(x)=c(y\rangle \leftrightarrow x\approx y and (ii) c(x)\approx x. Jech [1973b] p 154.

[97 A] For every set \{X_{i}:i\in I\} of local cardinal numbers, there is a set \{x_{i}:i\in I\} of sets such that for each i\in I there exists a y_{i}\in X_{i} such that x_{i}\approx y_{i}. (X is a local cardinal number if for all x, y\in X, x\approx y.) Higasikawa [1995].
FORM 98. The set of all finite subsets of a Dedekind finite set is Dedekind finite. Jech [1973b] p 161 prob 11.5 and note 94.

FORM 99. Rado’s Selection Lemma: Let \{K(\lambda ):\lambda \in \Lambda \} be a family of finite subsets (of X) and suppose for each finite S\subseteq \Lambda there is a function \gamma (S):S\rightarrow X such that (\forall \lambda \in S)(\gamma (S)(\lambda )\in K(\lambda )). Then there is an f:\Lambda \rightarrow X such that for every finite S\subseteq \Lambda there is a finite T such that S\subseteq T\subseteq \Lambda and such that f and \gamma (T) agree on S. Rado [1949].

[99 A] Weak Rado Lemma: Let \Lambda be a set. Suppose that \gamma is a function with domain all finite subsets of \Lambda such that for each finite S\subseteq \Lambda ,\,\gamma (S):S\rightarrow \{0,1\}. Then there is a \phi defined on \Lambda with the property that for every finite S\subseteq \Lambda there is a finite T\subseteq \Lambda such that S\subseteq T and \gamma (T) and \phi agree on S. Schechter [1996a] and Howard [1993].

[99 B] Rado’s Lemma restricted to families of two element sets: Let \{k(\lambda ):\lambda \in \Lambda \} be a family of 2 element subsets of a set X and suppose that for each finite S\subseteq \Lambda , there is a function \gamma (S) from S into X such that (\forall \lambda \in S)(\gamma (S)(\lambda )\in k(\lambda )). Then there is a function from \Lambda into X such that for every finite S\subseteq \Lambda , there is a finite T with S\subseteq T\subseteq \Lambda such that f and \gamma (T) agree on S. Rav [1977] and Howard [1993].
[99 C] Strong Rado Lemma 2: Let T be a family of finite sets and let \mathcal{F} be a collection of finite subsets of T satisfying
(1) (\forall K\in T)(\exists S\in \mathcal{F})(K\in S)
(2) (\forall S_{1}, S_{2}\in \mathcal{F})(S_{1}\cup S_{2}\in \mathcal{F})

Assume there is a function \phi with domain \mathcal{F} such that for each S\in \mathcal{F},\,\phi (S)= \phi _{S} is a function with domain S and satisfies (\forall K\in S)(\phi _{S}(K)\in K). Then there is a function f with domain T and with the following property: For all S\in \mathcal{F} there is an S^{\prime }\in \mathcal{F} such that S\subseteq S^{\prime } and f and \phi _{S^{\prime }} agree on S. Howard [1993].
FORM 100. Weak Partition Principle: For all sets x and y, if x\precsim ^{\ast }y, then it is not the case that y\prec x. Lindenbaum/Tarski [1926] and note 69.
[100 A] For every set A and function f it is false that A\prec f^{\prime \prime }A. G. Moore [1982], p. 327.
[100 B] For all sets x and y, if x\precsim ^{\ast }y and y\precsim x, then x\approx y. Higasikawa [1995] and note 69.
FORM 101. Partition Principle: If S is a partition of M, then S\precsim M. Sierpiński [1947].
[101 A] For all sets x and y,\,x\precsim ^{\ast }y implies x\precsim y. Lindenbaum/Tarski [1926] and note 69.
FORM 102. For all Dedekind finite cardinals p and q, if p^{2}=q^{2} then p=q. Jech [1973b] p 162 prob 11.12 and note 94.
FORM 103. If (P, <) is a linear ordering and |P|>\aleph _{1} then some initial segment of P is uncountable. Jech [1973b] p 164 prob 11.21.
FORM 104. There is a regular uncountable aleph. Jech [1966b] p 165 prob 11.26.

FORM 105. There is a partially ordered set (A, \leq ) such that for no set B is (B, \leq ) (the ordering on B is the usual injective cardinal ordering) isomorphic to (A, \leq ). Forti/Honsell [1985] and Jech [1966].
FORM 106. Baire Category Theorem for Compact Hausdorff Spaces: Every compact Hausdorff space is Baire. Goldblatt [1985], G. Moore [1982], and note 28.

[106 A] DMC: Dependent Multiple Choice: Every tree in which every element has at least one immediate successor has a subtree whose levels are finite and in which every element has at least one immediate successor. Blass [1979], Brunner [1983b], Fossy/Morillon [1995] and note 21.

[106 B] Weak DC: If R is a binary relation on a non-empty set E such that (\forall x\in E)(\exists y\in E)(x\,R\,y), then there is a sequence \langle F_{n}\rangle _{n\in \omega } of non-empty finite subsets of E such that (\forall n\in \omega )(\forall x\in F_{n})(\exists y\in F_{n+1})(x\,R\,y). (This statement remains equivalent to form 106 if we replace “binary relation” by “transitive binary relation”.) Fossy/Morillon [1995].
[106 C] Every scattered compact space is a Baire space. Fossy/Morillon [1995] and note 28.

[106 D] For every compact \mathrm{T}_{2} space (X, T) and every family D=\{D_{i}:i\in \omega \} of dense open sets of X there is a regular filter base \mathcal{F}\subseteq T (that is, if F,\,G\in \mathcal{F}, then there exists Q\in \mathcal{F} such that \overline{Q}\subseteq F\cap G) such that for all i\in \omega , for all but finitely many F\in \mathcal{F},\,\overline{F}\subset D_{i}. Fossy/Morillon [1995]
FORM 107. M. Hall’s Theorem: Let \{S(\alpha ):\alpha \in A\} be a collection of finite subsets (of a set X) then if

then there is an injective choice function on A. (That is, a 1-1 function f such that (\forall \alpha \in A)(f(\alpha )\in S(\alpha )).) (According to a theorem of P. Hall (\ast ) is equivalent to |\bigcup _{\alpha \in F}S(\alpha )|\geq |F|. P. Hall’s theorem does not require the axiom of choice.) M. Hall [1948].
FORM 108. There is an ordinal \alpha such that 2^{\aleph _{\alpha }} is not the union of a denumerable set of denumerable sets. Gitik [1985].

FORM 109. Every field F and every vector space V over F has the property that each linearly independent set A\subseteq V can be extended to a basis. Bleicher [1964], [1965], Blass [1984a], H. Rubin/J. Rubin [1985], pp 119 ff.
FORM 110. Every vector space over \mathbb{Q} has a basis. Blass [1984a].
FORM 111. UT(WO, 2, WO): The union of an infinite well ordered set of 2-element sets is an infinite well ordered set.
[111 A] C(WO, 2): Every well ordered family of 2-element sets has a choice function.

FORM 112. MC(\infty , LO): For every family X of non-empty sets each of which can be linearly ordered there is a function f such that for all y\in X,\,f(y) is a non-empty finite subset of y. Howard/Rubin [1977].
FORM 113. Tychonoff’s Compactness Theorem for Countably Many Spaces: The product of a countable set of compact spaces is compact. Brunner [1985a].

FORM 114. Every A-bounded T_{2} topological space is weakly Loeb. (A-bounded means amorphous subsets are relatively compact. Weakly Loeb means the set of non-empty closed subsets has a multiple choice function.) Brunner [1985a].
FORM 115. The product of weakly Loeb T_{2} spaces is weakly Loeb. (See form 114 for the definition of weakly Loeb.) Brunner [1985a].
FORM 116. Every compact T_{2} space is weakly Loeb. (See form 114 for the definition of weakly Loeb.) Brunner [1985a].
FORM 117. If \kappa is a measurable cardinal, then \kappa is the \kappa th inaccessible cardinal. Keisler/Tarski [1964] and note 20.
FORM 118. Every linearly orderable topological space is normal. Birkhoff [1967] p 241.
[118 A] For each complete linear order, the set of non-empty convex subsets has a choice function. van Douwen [1985].
[118 B] For each complete linear order, each pairwise disjoint collection of non-empty, convex, open subsets has a choice function. van Douwen [1985].
[118 C] Every linearly orderable space is collectionwise normal. van Douwen [1985] and note 71.
[118 D] Every linearly orderable space is collectionwise Hausdorff. van Douwen [1985] and note 71.
[118 E] Every linearly orderable space satisfies Urysohn’s lemma, van Douwen [1985] and note 141.
[118 F] Every linearly orderable space satisfies the Tietze-Urysohn extension theorem, van Douwen [1985] and note 141.

[118 G] Each complete linear order admits an extreme choice, that is, if (X, \leq ) is a linear order then there is a choice function f on the set of non-empty open interval of X with the property that for all (a, b, c)\in X^{3} with a<b<c,\,f((a, c))\in \{f((a, b)), b, f((b, c))\}. Morillon [1991a].
[118 H] For each linear order (X, \leq ), there is an ordinal \alpha and a strictly increasing injective map j from (X, \leq ) to \{0,1\}^{\alpha } with the lexicographic order. Morillon [1987].
[118 I] Every linearly ordered set of linear orders, each of which is non-empty and conditionally complete, has a choice function. Morillon [1988], van Douwen [1985], and note 71.
[118 J] If (X, \leq ) is a linear, complete order, then the order topology on X is hereditarily normal. Morillon [1988], van Douwen [1985], and note 71.
[118 K] If (X, \leq ) is a linear order, then the order topology on X is highly separated. Morillon [1988] and note 71.
[118 L] If X is a linear, complete order, then the order topology on X is highly separated. Morillon [1988] and note 71.

[118 M] If (X, \leq ) is a linear order, then the family \{A(a, b):a, b\in X\wedge a<b\} has a choice function. (A(a, b) denotes the set of continuous, order preserving functions from X into [0,1] such that f(a)=0 and f(b)=1.) Morillon [1988] and note 71.

[118 N] If (X, \leq ) is a linear order then the family \{A^{\prime }(a, b):a, b\in X\wedge a<b\} has a choice function. (A^{\prime }(a, b) denotes the set of continuous functions from X into [0,1] such that f(a)=0 and f(b)=1.) Morillon [1988] and note 71.
[118 O] If (X, \leq ) is a linear order, then the order topology on X is effectively normal. Morillon [1988] and note 71.
[118 P] If (X, \leq ) is a complete linear order, then the order topology on X is effectively normal. Morillon [1988] and note 71.
[118 Q] If (X, \leq ) is a linear order, then the order topology on X is hereditarily normal. Morillon [1988] and note 71.
[118 R] If (X, \leq ) is a linear order, then the order topology on X is monotonely normal. Morillon [1987] and note 71.

[118 S] If (X, \leq ) is a complete linear order then there is a choice function \ast for the family of non-empty open intervals of X such that if a,\,b,\,c\in X and either (a, b)\neq \emptyset or (b, c)\neq \emptyset then \ast ((a, c))\in \{\ast ((a, b)), \ast ((b, c)), b, b^{+}\} (where b^{+} is the successor of b if it exists and b otherwise). Morillon [1987] and note 71.
[118 T] Every complete linear order has an increasing choice function. Morillon [1987] and note 71.

[118 U] Every linearly ordered space is monotonically normal. (A space (X, <) is monotonically normal if there is an operator V which assigns to each x\in X and basic open neighborhood U of x a basic open neighborhood V(x, U) of x such that V(x, U)\cap V(x^{\prime }, U^{\prime })\neq \emptyset implies x\in U^{\prime } or x^{\prime }\in U.) Good/Tree [1995].

[118 V] If (L, \leq ) is a linear order and G=\{[l_{i}, r_{i}]:i\in K\} is a locally finite family of closed intervals of L whose interiors are non-empty and pairwise disjoint, then there exists a continuous real valued function f:L\rightarrow \mathbb{R} such that |f^{-1}(0) \cap [l_{i}, r_{i}]|\geq 2 and |f^{-1}(1) \cap [l_{i}, r_{i}]|\geq 1 for all i\in K. Keremedis [1995] and note 43.

[118 W] If (L, \leq ) is a linear order and G=\{[l_{i}, r_{i}]:i\in K\} is a locally finite family of closed intervals of L whose interiors are non-empty and pairwise disjoint, then there exists a continuous real valued function f:L\rightarrow \mathbb{R} such that for each i\in K,\,f(l_{i})=f(r_{i})=0 and f(x)>0 for all x\in (l_{i}, r_{i}). Keremedis [1995] and note 43.

[118 X] If (L, \leq ) is a complete linear order and G=\{(l_{i}, r_{i}):i\in K\} is a family of open, non-empty, pairwise disjoint intervals of L, then there exists a set \{f_{i}:i\in K\} of non constant continuous real valued functions on L such that for each i\in K,\,f_{i} vanishes outside of (l_{i}, r_{i}). Keremedis [1995].

FORM 119. C(\aleph _{0}, uniformly orderable with order type of the integers): Suppose \{A_{i}:i\in \omega \} is a set and there is a function f such that for each i\in \omega ,\,f(i) is an ordering of A_{i} of type \omega ^{\ast }+\omega (the usual ordering of the integers), then \{A_{i}:i\in \omega \} has a choice function. van Douwen [1985].
FORM 120(K). If K\subseteq \omega -\{0,1\},\, C(LO, K): Every linearly ordered set of non-empty sets each of whose cardinality is in K has a choice function. Truss [1973a].
FORM 121. C(LO, <\aleph _{0}): Every linearly ordered set of non-empty finite sets has a choice function. Truss [1973a].
FORM 122. C(WO, <\aleph _{0}): Every well ordered set of non-empty finite sets has a choice function. Truss [1973a].

[122 A] UT(WO, <\aleph _{0}, WO)\ (U_{\aleph _{0}}): The union of a well ordered set of finite sets is well orderable. Brunner/Howard [1992]. (See note 27 for more information on UT(WO, \kappa , WO), \kappa a well ordered cardinal. The proof that 122 implies [122 A] is similar to the proof given in Shannon [1988] p 569.)
FORM 123. SPI^{\ast }: Uniform weak ultrafilter principle: For each family F of infinite sets \exists f such that \forall x\in F,\,f(x) is a non-principal ultrafilter on x. Halpern [1972a]
[123 A] Form 70 + form 344. Morillon [1988].

FORM 124. Every operator on a Hilbert space with an amorphous base is the direct sum of a finite matrix and a scalar operator. (A set is amorphous if it is not the union of two disjoint infinite sets.) Brunner [1984a].
FORM 125. There does not exist an infinite, compact connected p space. (A p space is a T_{2} space in which the intersection of any well orderable family of open sets is open.) Brunner [1984c].

FORM 126. MC(\aleph _{0}, \infty ), Countable axiom of multiple choice: For every denumerable set X of non-empty sets there is a function f such that for all y\in X,\,f(y) is a non-empty finite subset of y. Brunner [1984d] and Blass [1979].
[126 A] Every positive functional on a B-lattice is continuous. Brunner [1984d] and note 16.
[126 B] Form 131 + form 350. Keremedis [1996] and note 132.
[126 C] FSCB + form 131. FSCB is “Every separable first countable space (X, T) has a denumerable \pi -base.” Keremedis [1996] and note 132.
[126 D] For every denumerable family A of disjoint non-empty sets there is an infinite set C\subset \bigcup A such that for every a\in A,\, 0\leq |C\cap a|<\omega . Keremedis [1996] and note 132.

[126 E] If (X, T) is a topological space, then for every family D=\{D_{i}:i\in \omega \} of dense open sets of X, there is a countable dense set S\subseteq X such that for all i\in \omega and for all but finitely many s\in S,\,s\in D_{i}. Keremedis [1996] and note 132.
[126 F] Every denumerable family of sets having the sfip also has a pseudointersection. Keremedis [1996] and note 132.
[126 G] DUN(w): The countable disjoint union of normal topological spaces is normal. Howard/Keremedis/Rubin/Rubin [1997a] and note 141.

[126 H] DUU(w): If C is a countable collection of pairwise disjoint topological spaces each of which satisfies Urysohn’s lemma, then the disjoint union of the spaces in C satisfies Urysohn’s lemma. Howard/Keremedis/Rubin/Rubin [1997a] and note 141.

[126 I] DUT(\omega ): If C is a countable collection of pairwise disjoint topological spaces each of which satisfies the Tietze-Urysohn extension theorem, then the disjoint union of the spaces in C satisfies the Tietze-Urysohn extension theorem. Howard/Keremedis/Rubin/Rubin [1997a] and note 141.
[126 J] F_{\sigma } subsets of paracompact spaces are paracompact. Howard/Keremedis/Rubin/Rubin [1997b] and note 141.
[126 K] F_{\sigma } subsets of metacompact spaces are metacompact. Howard/Keremedis/Rubin/Rubin [1997b] and note 141.
FORM 127. An amorphous power of a compact T_{2} space, which as a set is well orderable, is well orderable. Brunner [1984b].
FORM 128. Aczel’s Realization Principle: On every infinite set there is a Hausdorff topology with an infinite set of non-isolated points. Brunner [1984f].

FORM 129. For every infinite set A,\,A admits a partition into sets of order type \omega ^{\ast }+\omega . (For every infinite A, there is a set \{\langle C_{j}, <j\rangle :j\in J\} such that \{C_{j}:j\in J\} is a partition of A and for each j\in J, <_{j} is an ordering of C_{j} of type \omega ^{\ast }+\omega .) Brunner [1984f].
FORM 130. \mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}) is well orderable. Brunner [1984f].

FORM 131. MC_{\omega }(\aleph _{0}, \infty ): For every denumerable family X of pairwise disjoint non-empty sets, there is a function f such that for each x\in X,\,\mathrm{f(x)} is a non-empty countable subset of x. Howard/Keremedis/Rubin/Rubin [1997b].
FORM 132. PC(\infty <\aleph _{0}, \infty ): Every infinite family of finite sets has an infinite subfamily with a choice function. Blass [1977] and Kleinberg [1969].
[132 A] Every set mapping f:X\rightarrow [X]^{WO} (well orderable subsets of X) on a Dedekind finite, infinite set X has an infinite free subset. Brunner [1989]. notes 22 and 94.
FORM 133. Every set is either well orderable or has an infinite amorphous subset. Brunner [1982a].
FORM 134. If X is an infinite T_{1} space and X^{Y} is T_{5}, then Y is countable. (T_{5} is “hereditarily T_{4}”.) A. H. Stone [1948].

FORM 135. If X is a T_{2} space with at least two points and X^{Y} is hereditarily metacompact then Y is countable. (A space is metacompact if every open cover has an open point finite refinement. If B and B^{\prime } are covers of a space X, then B^{\prime } is a refinement of B if (\forall x\in B^{\prime })(\exists y\in B)(x\subseteq y). B is point finite if (\forall t\in X) there are only finitely many x\in B such that t\in x.) van Douwen [1980].
FORM 136(k). Surjective Cardinal Cancellation (depends on k\in \omega -\{0\}): For all cardinals x and y,\,kx\leq ^{\ast }ky implies x\leq ^{\ast }y. Truss [1984] and note 69.

FORM 137(k). Suppose k\in \omega -\{0\}. If f is a 1-1 map from k\times X into k\times Y then there are partitions X=\bigcup _{i<k}X_{i} and Y=\bigcup _{i<k}Y_{i} of X and Y such that f maps \bigcup _{i<k}(\{i\}\times X_{i}) onto \bigcup _{i<k}(\{i\}\times Y_{i}). Truss [1984].
[137 A(k)] For all X and Y\subseteq \mathbb{R} form 137(k) holds. Truss [1984]

FORM 138(k). Suppose k\in \omega . If f is a partial map from k\times Y onto k\times X (that is, the domain is a subset of k\times Y), then there are partitions X=\bigcup _{i<k}X_{i} and Y=\bigcup _{i<k}Y_{i} of X and Y such that f maps \bigcup _{i<k}(\{i\}\times Y_{i}) onto \bigcup _{i<k}(\{i\}\times X_{i}). Truss [1984].
[138 A(k)] For all standard X and Y, form 138(k) holds. Truss [1984]. This is equivalent to 138(k) in \mathrm{ZF}^{0}.
FORM 139. Using the discrete topology on 2, 2^{\mathcal{P}(\omega )} is compact. Truss [1984].

FORM 140. Let \Omega be the set of all (undirected) infinite cycles of reals (Graphs whose vertices are real numbers, connected, no loops and each vertex adjacent to exactly two others). Then there is a function f on \Omega such that for all s\in \Omega ,\,f(s) is a direction along s. Truss [1984].

[140 A] (Form 137 with k=2): If f is a 1-1 map from 2\times X into 2\times Y then there are partitions X=X_{0}\cup X_{1} and Y=Y_{0}\cup Y_{1} of X and Y such that f maps (\{0\}\times X_{0})\cup (\{1\}\times X_{1}) onto (\{0\}\times Y_{0})\cup (\{1\}\times Y_{1}). Truss [1984].

FORM 141. [14\ \mathrm{P}(n)] with n=2: Let \{A(i):i\in I\} be a collection of sets such that \forall i\in I,\ |A(i)|\leq 2 and suppose R is a symmetric binary relation on \bigcup _{i\in I}A(i) such that for all finite W\subseteq I there is an R consistent choice function for \{A(i):i\in W\}. Then there is an R consistent choice function for \{A(i):i\in I\}. Cowen [1977b] and note 109.
FORM 142. \neg PB: There is a set of reals without the property of Baire. Jech [1973b] p 7 and note 28.
FORM 143. H(C, TR): If (X, R) is a connected relation (u\neq v\rightarrow u\ R\ v or v\ R\ u) then X contains a \subseteq -maximal transitive subset. Harper/Rubin [1976] and note 39.
FORM 144. Every set is almost well orderable. Keisler [1970] and note 25.
[144 A] Every p space is discrete. (A p space is a T_{2} space in which the intersection of any well orderable family of open sets is open). Brunner [1984c].
FORM 145. Compact P_{0}-spaces are Dedekind finite. (A P_{0}-space is a topological space in which the intersection of a countable collection of open sets is open.) Brunner [1984c] and note 94.

FORM 146. A(F, A1): For every T_{2} topological space (X, T), if X is a continuous finite to one image of an A1 space then (X, T) is an A1 space. ((X, T) is A1 means if U\subseteq T covers X then \exists f:X\rightarrow U such that (\forall x\in X)(x\in f(x)).) Brunner [1983a] and note 26.
FORM 147. A(D2): Every T_{2} topological space (X, T) can be covered by a well ordered family of discrete sets. Brunner [1983a] and note 26.
FORM 148. A(W2, B1): For every T_{2} topological space (X, T), if X is well ordered, then X has a well ordered base. Brunner [1983a] and note 26.
FORM 149. A(F): Every T_{2} topological space is a continuous, finite to one image of an A1 space. Brunner [1983a] and note 26.
FORM 150. PC(\infty , \aleph _{0}, \infty ): Every infinite set of denumerable sets has an infinite subset with a choice function.

FORM 151. UT(WO, \aleph _{0}, WO)\ (U_{\aleph _{1}}): The union of a well ordered set of denumerable sets is well orderable. Brunner/Howard [1992]. (If \kappa is a well ordered cardinal, see note 27 for UT(WO, \kappa , WO).)

FORM 152. D_{\aleph _{0}}: Every non-well-orderable set is the union of a pairwise disjoint, well orderable family of denumerable sets. Brunner/Howard [1992]. (See note 27 for D_{\kappa },\,\kappa a well ordered cardinal.)
FORM 153. The closed unit ball of a Hilbert space is compact in the weak topology. Fossy/Morillon [1995] and Rudin [1991].
FORM 154. Tychonoff’s Compactness Theorem for Countably Many T_{2} Spaces: The product of countably many T_{2} compact spaces is compact. Brunner [1983b].

FORM 155. LC: There are no non-trivial Läuchli continua. (A Läuchli continuum is a strongly connected continuum. Continuum \equiv compact, connected, Hausdorff space; and strongly connected \equiv every continuous real valued function is constant.) Brunner [1983] and Läuchli [1962].

FORM 156. Theorem of Gelfand and Kolmogoroff: Two compact T_{2} spaces are homeomorphic if their rings of real valued continuous functions are isomorphic. Brunner [1983] and Gelfand/Kolmogoroff [1939].

FORM 157. Theorem of Goodner: A compact T_{2} space is extremally disconnected (the closure of every open set is open) if and only if each non-empty subset of C(X) (set of continuous real valued functions on X) which is pointwise bounded has a supremum. Goodner [1950].
FORM 158. In every Hilbert space H, if the closed unit ball is sequentially compact, then H has an orthonormal basis. Brunner [1983a].
FORM 159. The regular cardinals are cofinal in the class of ordinals. Blass [1983a].
[159 A] Every variety has an initial algebra. Blass [1983a] and note 32.
[159 B] For every variety V and set X,\,V has a free algebra on X. Blass [1983a] and note 32.
FORM 160. No Dedekind finite set can be mapped onto an aleph. (See [9 E].) Monro [1975] and note 94.
FORM 161. Definability of cardinal addition in terms of \leq : There is a first order formula whose only non-logical symbol is \leq (for cardinals) that defines cardinal addition. Häussler [1983].
FORM 162. Non-existence of infinite units: There is no infinite cardinal number A such that A+A>A and for all cardinals x and y,\,x+y=A\rightarrow x=A or y=A. Häussler [1983].
FORM 163. Every non-well-orderable set has an infinite, Dedekind finite subset. Brunner [1982a] and note 94.
FORM 164. Every non-well-orderable set has an infinite subset with a Dedekind finite power set. Brunner [1982a], notes 42 and 94.
FORM 165. C(WO, WO): Every well ordered family of non-empty, well orderable sets has a choice function.
FORM 166. PC(\infty , 2, \infty ): Every infinite family of pairs has an infinite subfamily with a choice function. Brunner [1982a].

FORM 167. PKW(\aleph _{0}, \geq 2, \infty ), Partial Kinna-Wagner Principle: For every denumerable family F such that for all x\in F,\,|x|\geq 2, there is an infinite subset H\subseteq F and a function f such that for all x\in H,\,\emptyset \neq f(x)\subsetneq x. Brunner [1982a].
FORM 168. Dual Cantor-Bernstein Theorem: (\forall x)(\forall y)(|x|\leq ^{\ast }|y| and |y|\leq ^{\ast }|x| implies |x|=|y|). Banaschewski/Moore [1990] and note 69.
FORM 169. There is an uncountable subset of \mathbb{R} without a perfect subset. Banaschewski/Moore [1990], Bernstein [1908], and note 28.
FORM 170. \aleph _{1}\leq 2^{\aleph _{0}}. Bernstein [1908] and Banaschewski/Moore [1990].
[170 A] There is a function that assigns to each denumerable set D of real numbers a real number not in D. Sierpiński [1954].
[170 B] There is an uncountable, well orderable set of reals. Raisonnier [1982] and note 3.

FORM 171. If (P, \leq ) is a partial order such that P is the denumerable union of finite sets and all antichains in P are finite then for each denumerable family \mathcal{D} of dense sets there is a \mathcal{D} generic filter. Shannon [1990] and note 47.
FORM 172. For every infinite set S, if S is hereditarily countable (that is, every y\in TC(S) is countable) then |TC(S)|=\aleph _{0}. Jech [1982].
FORM 173. MPL: Metric spaces are para-Lindelöf. Howard/Keremedis/Rubin/ Stanley [1997] and note 141.
[173 A] MML: Metric spaces are meta-Lindelöf. Howard/Keremedis/Rubin/ Stanley [1997] and note 141.

FORM 174(\alpha ). RM1,\,\aleph _{\alpha }: The representation theorem for multi-algebras with \aleph _{\alpha } unary operations: Assume (A, F) is a multi-algebra with \aleph _{\alpha } unary operations (and no other operations). Then there is an algebra (B, G) with \aleph _{\alpha } unary operations and an equivalence relation E on B such that (B/E, G/E) and (A, F) are isomorphic multi-algebras. Höft/Howard [1981] and note 50.
FORM 175. Transitivity Condition: For all sets x, there is a set u abd a function f such that u is transitive and f is a one to one function from x onto u. von Rimscha [1982].
FORM 176. Every infinite, locally finite group has an infinite Abelian subgroup. (Locally finite means every finite subset generates a finite subgroup.) Plotkin [1981].
FORM 177. An infinite box product of regular T_{1} spaces, each of cardinality greater than 1, is neither first countable nor connected. Brunner [1981a], Knight [1964], and note 52.

FORM 178(n, N). If n\in \omega , n\geq 2 and N\subseteq \{1,2, \ldots , n-1\},\, N\neq \emptyset ,\, MC(\infty , n, N): If X is any set of n-element sets then there is a function f with domain X such that for all A\in X,\,f(A)\subseteq A and |f(A)|\in N. Zuckerman [1969a], [1981], and note 53.
FORM 179(\epsilon ). Suppose \epsilon >0 is an ordinal. \forall x, x\in W(\epsilon ). David [1980] and note 25.

FORM 180. Every Abelian group has a divisible hull. (If A and B are groups, B is a divisible hull of A means B is a divisible group, A is a subgroup of B and for every non-zero b\in B,\, \exists n\in \omega such that 0\neq nb\in A.) Fuchs [1970], Theorem 24.4 p 107, Hodges [1980], and note 24.
FORM 181. C(2^{\aleph _{0}}, \infty ): Every set X of non-empty sets such that |X|=2^{\aleph _{0}} has a choice function. Freyd [1980].
FORM 182. There is an aleph whose cofinality is greater than \aleph _{0}. Gitik [1980].
FORM 183(\alpha ). There are no \aleph _{\alpha } minimal sets. That is, there are no sets X such that
(1) |X| is incomparable with \aleph _{\alpha }
(2) \aleph _{\beta }<|X| for every \beta <\alpha and
(3) \forall Y\subseteq X,\,|Y|<\aleph _{\alpha } or |X-Y|<\aleph _{\alpha }.
Hickman [1980b] and note 56.
FORM 184. Existence of a double uniformization: For all X and Y, for all E\subseteq X\times Y, if there is an infinite cardinal \kappa satisfying:
(1) \forall y_{0}\in Y,\,|\{(x, y_{0}):x\in X\}\cap E|=\kappa and
(2) \forall x_{0}\in X,\,|\{(x_{0}, y):y\in Y\}\cap E|=\kappa ,

then \exists U\subseteq E such that for all (x, y)\in E,\,\exists !z\in X such that (z, y)\in U and \exists !z\in Y such that (x, z)\in U. (U is called a double uniformization of E.) Kaniewski/Rogers [1980].
FORM 185. Every linearly ordered Dedekind finite set is finite. Hickman [1979a] and note 94.
[185 A] If X is a linearly ordered set and there is neither an increasing nor a decreasing injection f:\omega \rightarrow X, then X is finite. Hickman [1979a].
FORM 186. Every pair of cardinal numbers has a least upper bound (in the usual cardinal ordering.) Hickman [1979b].
FORM 187. Every pair of cardinal numbers has a greatest lower bound (in the usual cardinal ordering.) Hickman [1979b].
FORM 188. EP Ab: For every Abelian group A there is a projective Abelian group G and a homomorphism from G onto A. Blass [1979] and note 60.
FORM 189. EI Ab: For every Abelian group A there is an injective Abelian group G and a one to one homomorphism from A into G. Blass [1979] and note 60.
FORM 190. There is a non-trivial injective Abelian group. Blass [1979] and note 60.
FORM 191. SVC: There is a set S such that for every set a, there is an ordinal \alpha and a function from S\times \alpha onto a. Blass [1979].
FORM 192. EP sets: For every set A there is a projective set X and a function from X onto A. Blass [1979] and note 60.
[192 A] (\forall x)(\exists y) (x\leq ^{\ast }y and y indexed choice holds). Blass in Mathias [1977b], notes 60 and 69.
FORM 193. EFP Ab: Every Abelian group is a homomorphic image of a free projective Abelian group. Blass [1979] and note 60.

FORM 194. C(\varPi _{2}^{1}) or AC(\varPi _{2}^{1}): If P\in \omega \times ^{\omega } \omega ,\,P has domain \omega , and P is in \varPi _{2}^{1}, then there is a sequence of elements \langle x_{k}: k\in \omega \rangle of ^{\omega }\omega with \langle k,\,x_{k}\rangle \in P for all k\in \omega . Kanovei [1979] and note 61.
FORM 195. Every general linear system has a linear global reaction. Note 62 and Harazisville (see Kharazishvili [1979]).
FORM 196(\alpha ). \aleph _{\alpha } and \aleph _{\alpha +1} are not both measurable. Bull [1978] and note 20.
FORM 197. \mathbb{R}^{2} is the union of three sets C with the property that for all x\in C there is a straight line L such that L\cap C=\{x\}. Davies [1978].
FORM 198. For every set S, if the only linearly orderable subsets of S are the finite subsets of S, then either S is finite or S has an amorphous subset. Hickman [1978b] and note 57.

FORM 199(n). (For n\in \omega -\{0, 1\}) If all \varSigma _{n}^{1}, Dedekind finite subsets of ^{\omega }\omega are finite, then all \varPi _{n}^{1} Dedekind finite subsets of ^{\omega }\omega are finite. Kanovei [1978], notes 57 and 61.
FORM 200. For all infinite x,\,|2^{x}|=|x!|. Dawson/Howard [1976] and note 64.
FORM 201. Linking Axiom for Boolean Algebras: Every Boolean algebra has a maximal linked system. (L\subseteq B is linked if a\wedge b\neq 0 for all a and b\in L.) Schrijver [1978].

[201 A] Strong Linking Axiom for Boolean Algebras: Each linked system in a Boolean algebra is contained in some maximal linked system. (If B is a Boolean algebra, L\subseteq B is linked if a\wedge b\neq 0 for all a and b\in L.) Schrijver [1978].

[201 B] Disjoint Transversal axiom (2,2): If X is a set and \mathcal{U} and \mathcal{V} are subsets of \{y\subseteq X:|y|\leq 2\} and if for each two finite subsets \mathcal{U}_{0}\subseteq \mathcal{U} and \mathcal{V}_{0}\subseteq \mathcal{V} there are transversals Y_{1} and Y_{2} for \mathcal{U}_{0} and \mathcal{V}_{0} respectively such that Y_{1}\cap Y_{2}=\emptyset , then there are disjoint transversals X_{1} and X_{2} for \mathcal{U} and \mathcal{V} respectively. (Y\subseteq X is a transversal for \mathcal{U} if for all y\in CalU,\, y\cap Y\neq \emptyset .) Schrijver [1978].
FORM 202. C(LO, \infty ): Every linearly ordered family of non-empty sets has a choice function. Truss [1978].
[202 A] H(TR\& C, P): If (X, R) is a transitive, connected relation. Then X has a \subseteq -maximal partially ordered subset. Harper/Rubin [1976] and note 39.
FORM 203. C(disjoint,\subseteq \mathbb{R}): Every partition of \mathcal{P}(\omega ) into non-empty subsets has a choice function. Truss [1978].
FORM 204. For every infinite X, there is a function from X onto 2X. Truss [1978].
FORM 205. For all cardinals m and n, if m\leq ^{\ast }n and \neg (n\leq ^{\ast }m) then there is a cardinal k<n such that m\leq ^{\ast }k. Pelc [1978] and note 69.
FORM 206. The existence of a non-principal ultrafilter: There exists an infinite set X and a non-principal ultrafilter on X. Blass [1977b].

FORM 207(\alpha ). UT(\aleph _{\alpha }, \aleph _{\alpha }, <2^{\aleph _{\alpha }}): The union of \aleph _{\alpha } sets each of cardinality \aleph _{\alpha } has cardinality less than 2^{\aleph _{\alpha }}. Figura [1977].
FORM 208. For all ordinals \alpha ,\,\aleph _{\alpha +1}\leq 2^{\aleph _{\alpha }}. Figura [1977].

FORM 209. There is an ordinal \alpha such that for all X, if X is a denumerable union of denumerable sets then \mathcal{P}(X) cannot be partitioned into \aleph _{\alpha } non-empty sets. Morris [1970].
FORM 210. The commutator subgroup of a free group is free. Läuchli [1962].

FORM 211. DCR: Dependent choice for relations on \mathbb{R}: If R\subseteq \mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{R} satisfies (\forall x\in \mathbb{R})(\exists y\in \mathbb{R})(x\,R\,y) then there is a sequence \langle x(n): n\in \omega \rangle of real numbers such that (\forall n\in \omega )(x(n)\, R\, x(n+1)). Mathias [1977].

FORM 212. C(2^{\aleph _{0}}, \subseteq \mathbb{R}): If R is a relation on \mathbb{R} such that for all x\in \mathbb{R}, there is a y\in \mathbb{R} such that x\,R\,y, then there is a function f:\mathbb{R} \rightarrow \mathbb{R} such that for all x\in \mathbb{R},\,x\,R\,f(x). Mathias [1977].
FORM 213. C(\infty , \aleph _{1}): If (\forall y\in X)(|y|=\aleph _{1}) then X has a choice function. Pincus [1977].
FORM 214. Z(\omega ): For every family A of infinite sets, there is a function f such that for all y\in A,\,f(y) is a non-empty subset of y and |f(y)|=\aleph _{0}. Pincus [1977].
FORM 215. If (\forall y\subseteq X)(y can be linearly ordered implies y is finite), then X is finite. Pincus [1972].
FORM 216. Every infinite tree has either an infinite chain or an infinite antichain. Pincus [1972] and note 21.
FORM 217. Every infinite partially ordered set has either an infinite chain or an infinite antichain. Pincus [1972].

FORM 218. (\forall n\in \omega -\{0\})MC(\infty , \infty , relatively prime to n): \forall n\in \omega -\{0\}, if X is a set of non-empty sets, then there is a function f such that for all x\in X,\,f(x) is a non-empty, finite subset of x and |f(x)| is relatively prime to n. Bleicher [1965].

[218 A] Existence of Complementary Subspaces: For every field F, every vector space V over F has the property that if S\subseteq V is a subspace of V, then there is a subspace S^{\prime }\subseteq V such that S\cap S^{\prime }=\{0\} and S\cup S^{\prime } generates V. Bleicher [1964], [1965], H. Rubin/J. Rubin [1985], pp 123ff, Theorems 6.36, 6.37, and 6.38.

FORM 219. (\forall n\in \omega -\{0\})MC(\infty , WO, relatively prime to n): For all non-zero n\in \omega , if X is a set of non-empty well orderable sets, then there is a function f such that for all x\in X,\, f(x) is a non-empty, finite subset of x, and |f(x)| is relatively prime to n. Pincus [1972].
FORM 220(p). Suppose p\in \omega and p is a prime. Any two elementary Abelian p-groups (all non-trivial elements have order p) of the same cardinality are isomorphic. Hickman [1977b].
FORM 221. For all infinite X, there is a non-principal measure on \mathcal{P}(X). Pincus/Solovay [1977] and note 147.
FORM 222. There is a non-principal measure on \mathcal{P}(\omega ). Pincus/Solovay [1977] and note 147.
FORM 223. There is an infinite set X and a non-principal measure on \mathcal{P}(X). Pincus/Solovay [1977] and note 147.

FORM 224. There is a partition of the real line into \aleph _{1} Borel sets \{B_{\alpha }:\alpha <\aleph _{1}\} such that for some \beta <\aleph _{1},\,\forall \alpha <\aleph _{1},\, B_{\alpha }\in G_{\beta }. (G_{\beta } for \beta <\aleph _{1} is defined by induction, G_{0}={A: A is an open subset of \mathbb{R}} and for \beta >0,

inline-formula.tex-math: G_{\beta }=\{\bigcap _{i=0}^{\infty }A_{i}:(\forall i\in w)(\exists \xi <\beta )(A_{i}\in G_{\xi })\}\ \mathrm{if}\ \beta \ \mathrm{is\ even\ and}

sec.p: Stern [1979].
FORM 225. Every proper filter on \omega can be extended to an ultrafilter. Rav [1977].
[225 A] There exists a compact, extremally disconnected topological space having a Dedekind infinite set of clopen subsets. Morillon [1993], notes 94 and 114.
[225 B] There exists a compact, \sigma -extremally disconnected topological space having a Dedekind infinite set of clopen subsets. Morillon [1993], notes 94 and 114.

FORM 226. Let R be a commutative ring with identity, B a proper subring containing 1 and q a prime ideal in B. Then there is a subring A of R and a prime ideal p in A such that (a) B\subseteq A (b) q=B\cap p (c) R-p is multiplicatively closed and (d) if A\neq R, then R-A is multiplicatively closed. Rav [1977].
FORM 227. For all groups G, if every finite subgroup of G can be fully ordered then G can be fully ordered. Rav [1977] and note 79.
FORM 228. Every torsion free Abelian group can be fully ordered. Rav [1977] and note 79.

FORM 229. If (G, \circ , \leq ) is a partially ordered group, then \leq can be extended to a linear order on G if and only if for every finite set \{a_{1}, \ldots , a_{n}\}\subseteq G, with a_{i}\neq the identity for i=1 to n, the signs \epsilon _{1},\,\ldots ,\,\epsilon _{n}\ (\epsilon _{i}=\pm 1) can be chosen so that P\cap S(a_{1}^{\epsilon _{1}}, \ldots , a_{n}^{\epsilon _{n}})=\emptyset (where S(b_{1}, \ldots , b_{n}) is the normal sub-semi-group of G generated by b_{1},\,\ldots ,\,b_{n} and P=\{g\in G:e\leq g\} where e is the identity of G.) Rav [1977].
FORM 230. L^{1}=HOD. Szczepaniak [1977] and note 82.
FORM 231. UT(WO, WO, WO): The union of a well ordered collection of well orderable sets is well orderable. Tsukada [1977].
[231 A] Every almost well orderable set (W-set) is well orderable. Note 25.
FORM 232. Every metric space (X, d) has a \sigma -point finite base. Howard/ Keremedis/Rubin/Stanley [1997] and note 141.
[232 A] Every metric space has a \gamma -point finite base, for some ordinal \gamma . Howard/Keremedis/Rubin/Stanley [1997] and note 141.
[232 B] Every metric space has a \sigma -locally finite base. Howard/Keremedis/ Rubin/Stanley [1997] and note 141.
[232 C] Every metric space has a \gamma -locally finite base, for some ordinal \gamma . Howard/Keremedis/Rubin/Stanley [1997] and note 141.
[232 D] Every metric space (X, d) has a \sigma -discrete base. Howard/Keremedis/Rubin/Stanley [1997] and note 141.
[232 E] Every metric space (X, d) has a \gamma -discrete base, for some ordinal \gamma . Howard/Keremedis/Rubin/Stanley [1997] and note 141.
[232 F] Every metric space (X, d) has a \sigma -disjoint base. Howard/Keremedis/ Rubin/Stanley [1997] and note 141.
[232 G] Every metric space (X, d) has a \gamma -disjoint base for some ordinal \gamma . Howard/Keremedis/Rubin/Stanley [1997] and note 141.
FORM 233. If a field has an algebraic closure it is unique up to isomorphism. Mathias [1977b].

FORM 234. There is a non-Ramsey set: There is a set A of infinite subsets of \omega such that for every infinite subset N of \omega ,\,N has a subset which is in A and a subset which is not in A. Prikry [1976] and Mathias [1968].
FORM 235. If V is a vector space and B_{1} and B_{2} are bases for V then |B_{1}| and |B_{2}| are comparable. Gross [1976].
FORM 236. If V is a vector space with a basis and S is a linearly independent subset of V such that no proper extension of S is a basis for V, then S is a basis for V. Gross [1975], [1976].
[236 A] If V is a vector space with a basis, then every linearly independent subset is contained in a basis.
FORM 237. The order of any group is divisible by the order of any of its subgroups, (i.e., if H is a subgroup of G then there is a set A such that |H\times A|=|G|.) Hickman [1976].
FORM 238. Every elementary Abelian group (that is, for some prime p every non identity element has order p) is the direct sum of cyclic subgroups. Hickman [1976].
FORM 239. For all X, if X\neq \emptyset , then there is a binary operation on X that makes X a group. Hickman [1976].
FORM 240. If a group G satisfies “every ascending chain of subgroups is finite,” then every subgroup of G is finitely generated. Hickman [1976].
FORM 241. Every algebraic closure of \mathbb{Q} has a real closed subfield. Hodges [1976a], Läuchli [1962] and note 84.
FORM 242. There is, up to an isomorphism, at most one algebraic closure of \mathbb{Q}. Hodges [1976a], Läuchli [1962] and note 84.
FORM 243. Every principal ideal domain is a unique factorization domain. Hodges [1976a] and note 84.
FORM 244. Every principal ideal domain has a maximal ideal. Hodges [1976a] and note 84.
FORM 245. There is a function f:\omega _{1}\rightarrow \omega _{1}^{\omega } such that for every \alpha ,\, 0<\alpha <\omega _{1},\,f(\alpha ) is a function from \omega onto \alpha . Litman [1976].

[245 A] There is a function g:\omega _{1}\rightarrow \omega _{1}^{\omega } such that for all limit ordinals \alpha <\omega _{1},\,g(\alpha ) is an increasing function from \omega into \alpha with the range of g cofinal in \alpha . Litman [1976]

[245 B] Every closed set A in \omega _{1} which contains only limit ordinals is a derivative (that is, \exists B\subseteq \omega _{1} such that A=\{x:x is a limit and \{t:t\in B\} is cofinal in x\}.) Litman [1976].
FORM 246. The monadic theory theory MT(\omega _{1}, <) of \omega _{1} is recursive. Litman [1976] and note 85.
FORM 247. Every atomless Boolean algebra is Dedekind infinite. Plotkin [1976], notes 86 and 94.
FORM 248. For any \kappa ,\,\kappa is the cardinal number of an infinite complete Boolean algebra if and only if \kappa ^{\aleph _{0}}=\kappa . Plotkin [1976] and note 86.
FORM 249. If T is an infinite tree in which every element has exactly 2 immediate successors then T has an infinite branch. Truss [1975], note 87 and note 21.
FORM 250. (\forall n\in \omega -\{0,1\})(C(WO, n)): For every natural number n\geq 2, every well ordered family of n element sets has a choice function. Truss [1975].
FORM 251. The additive groups (\mathbb{R}, +) and (\mathbb{C}, +) are isomorphic. Ash [1975].
FORM 252. The additive groups of \mathbb{Q} \oplus \mathbb{R} and \mathbb{R} are isomorphic. Ash [1975].

FORM 253. Łoś’ Theorem: If M=\langle A,\,R_{j}\rangle _{j\in J} is a relational system, X any set and \mathcal{F} an ultrafilter in \mathcal{P}(X), then M and M^{X}/\mathcal{F} are elementarily equivalent. Howard [1975].
FORM 254. Z(D, R, l): Every directed relation (P, R) in which ramified subsets have least upper bounds, has a maximal element. Harper/Rubin [1976] and note 39.
FORM 255. Z(D, R): Every directed relation (P, R) in which every ramified subset A has an upper bound, has a maximal element. Harper/Rubin [1976] and note 39.
FORM 256. Z(P, F): Every partially ordered set (X, R) in which every forest A has an upper bound, has a maximal element. Harper/Rubin [1976] and note 39.
FORM 257. Z(TR, P): Every transitive relation (X, R) in which every partially ordered subset has an upper bound, has a maximal element. Harper/Rubin [1976] and note 39.
FORM 258. Z(D, L): Every directed relation (X, R) in which linearly ordered subsets have upper bounds, has a maximal element. Harper/Rubin [1976] and note 39.
FORM 259. Z(TR\& C, W): If (X,\, R) is a transitive and connected relation in which every well ordered subset has an upper bound, then (X, R) has a maximal element. Harper/Rubin [1976] and note 39.

FORM 260. Z(TR\& C, P): If (X, R) is a transitive and connected relation in which every partially ordered subset has an upper bound, then (X, R) has a maximal element. Harper/Rubin [1976] and note 39.
