FORM 261. Z(TR, T): Every transitive relation (X, R) in which every subset which is a tree has an upper bound, has a maximal element. Harper/Rubin [1976] and note 39.
FORM 262. Z(TR, R): Every transitive relation (X, R) in which every ramified subset A has an upper bound, has a maximal element. Harper/Rubin [1976] and note 39.
FORM 263. H(AS\& C, P): Every every relation (X, R) which is antisymmetric and connected contains a \subseteq -maximal partially ordered subset. Harper/Rubin [1976] and note 39.
FORM 264. H(C, P): Every connected relation (X, R) contains a \subseteq -maximal partially ordered set. Harper/Rubin [1976] and note 39.
FORM 265. H(A, TR): Every relation (X, R) contains a \subseteq -maximal transitive subset. Harper/Rubin [1976] and note 39.
FORM 266. H(AS, P): Every antisymmetric relation contains \subseteq -maximal partially ordered subset. Harper/Rubin [1976] and note 39.
FORM 267. There is no infinite, free complete Boolean algebra. Stavi [1975] and note 89.

FORM 268. If \mathcal{L} is a lattice isomorphic to the lattice of subalgebras of some unary universal algebra (a unary universal algebra is one with only unary or nullary operations) and \alpha is an automorphism of \mathcal{L} of order 2 (that is, \alpha ^{2} is the identity) then there is a unary algebra \mathfrak{A} and an isomorphism \rho from \mathcal{L} onto the lattice of subalgebras of \mathfrak{A}^{2} with \rho (\alpha (x))=(\rho (x))^{-1}(=\{(s, t):(t, s)\in \rho (x)\}\rangle for all x\in \mathcal{L}. Lampe [1974].
FORM 269. For every cardinal m, there is a set A such that 2^{|A|^{2}}\geq m and there is a choice function on the collection of 2-element subsets of A. Lampe [1974].
FORM 270. CT_{\mathrm{fin}}: The compactness theorem for propositional logic restricted to sets of formulas in which each variable occurs only in a finite number of formulas. Kolany/Wojtylak [1991].

[270 A] C(\infty , <\aleph _{0})\wedge CT_{2}\ (CT_{2} is the compactness theorem for propositional logic restricted to sets of formulas in which each variable occurs in at most two formulas. See form 271(n).) Kolany/Wojtylak [1991].

[270 B] F_{\mathrm{fin}}: For any family \mathcal{F} of pairwise disjoint, non-empty, finite sets if R is a symmetric binary relation on \bigcup \mathcal{F} which satisfies (i) the set \{b\in \bigcup \mathcal{F}:\neg a\,R\,b\} is finite for every a\in \bigcup \mathcal{F} and (ii) every finite subfamily of \mathcal{F} has an R-consistent choice function, then \mathcal{F} has an R-consistent choice function. Kolany/Wojtylak [1991].

[270 C(n)] F_{n}^{\mathrm{fin}} (n\geq 3 a natural number): For any family \mathcal{F} of pairwise disjoint, n element sets if R is a symmetric binary relation on \bigcup \mathcal{F} which satisfies (i) the set \{b\in \bigcup \mathcal{F}:\neg a\ R\ b\} is finite for every a\in \bigcup \mathcal{F} and (ii) every finite subfamily of \mathcal{F} has an R-consistent choice function, then \mathcal{F} has an R-consistent choice function. Kolany [1992].

FORM 271 (n). If n\in \omega -\{0,1\},\,CT_{n}: The compactness theorem for propositional logic restricted to sets of formulas in which each variable occurs in at most n formulas. Kolany/Wojtylak [1991].
FORM 272. There is an X\subseteq \mathbb{R} such that neither X nor \mathbb{R} -X has a perfect subset. Truss [1974b] and note 28.
FORM 273. There is a subset of \mathbb{R} which is not Borel. Truss [1974b].

FORM 274. There is a cardinal number x and an n\in \omega such that \neg (x\ \mathrm{adj}^{n}\,x^{2}). (The expression “x\,\mathrm{adj}^{n}\, ya^{\prime \prime } means there are cardinals z_{0},\,\ldots ,\,z_{n} such that z_{0}=x and z_{n}=y and for all i,\,0\leq i<n,\,z_{i}<z_{i+1} and if z_{i}<z\leq z_{i+1}, then z=z_{i+1}.) (Compare with [0 A]). Truss [1974b].
FORM 275. The sequence of cardinals \langle \aleph _{n}: n\in \omega \rangle has a unique minimal upper bound. Truss [1974b].
FORM 276. E(V^{\prime \prime }, III): For every set A,\,\mathcal{P}(A) is Dedekind finite if and only if A=\emptyset or 2|\mathcal{P}(A)|>|\mathcal{P}(A)|. Howard/Spis̆iak [1994] and note 94.
FORM 277. E(D, VII): Every non-well-orderable cardinal is decomposable. Monro [1973a] and note 94.
FORM 278. In an integral domain R, if every ideal is finitely generated then R has a maximal proper ideal. Hodges [1974] and note 45 E.

FORM 279. The Closed Graph Theorem for operations between Fréchet Spaces: Suppose X and Y are Fréchet spaces, T:X\rightarrow Y is linear and G=\{(x, Tx): x\in X\} is closed in X\times Y. Then T is continuous. Rudin [1991] p. 51, Wright [1973], note 96.
FORM 280. There is a complete separable metric space with a subset which does not have the Baire property. Wright [1973] and note 28.
FORM 281. There is a Hilbert space H and an unbounded linear operator on H. Wright [1973], note 96.
FORM 282. \omega \not \rightarrow (\omega )^{\omega }. Erdös/Rado [1952], Kleinberg/Seiferas [1973] and note 97.
FORM 283. Cardinality of well ordered subsets: For all n\in \omega and for all infinite x,\,|x^{n}|<|s(x)| where s(x) is the set of all well orderable subsets of x. Truss [1973].
FORM 284. A system of linear equations over a field F has a solution in F if and only if every finite sub-system has a solution in F. Cowen/Emerson [1995].

FORM 285. Let E be a set and f:E\rightarrow E, then f has a fixed point if and only if E is not the union of three mutually disjoint sets E_{1},\,E_{2} and E_{3} such that E_{i}\cap f(E_{i})=\emptyset for i=1,2,3. Makowski/Wiśniewski [1969], Abian [1968], Baker [1964], and Kenyon [1963].

FORM 286. Extended Krein-Milman Theorem: Let K be a quasicompact (sometimes called convex-compact), convex subset of a locally convex topological vector space, then K has an extreme point. H. Rubin/J. Rubin [1985], p. 177–178 and note 23.

FORM 287. The Hahn-Banach Theorem for Separable Normed Linear Spaces: Assume V is a separable normed linear space and p:V\rightarrow \mathbb{R} satisfies p(x+y)\leq p(x)+p(y) and (\forall t\geq 0)(\forall x\in V)(p(tx)=tp(x)) and assume f is a linear function from a subspace S of V into \mathbb{R} which satisfies (\forall x\in S)(f(x)\leq p(x)), then f can be extended to f^{\ast }:V\rightarrow \mathbb{R} so that f^{\ast } is linear and (\forall x\in V)(f^{\ast }(x)\leq p(x)). Note 145.
FORM 288(n). If n\in \omega -\{0,1\}, C(\aleph _{0}, n): Every denumerable set of n-element sets has a choice function. Wiśniewski [1972a].
FORM 289. If S is a set of subsets of a countable set and S is closed under chain unions, then S has a \subseteq -maximal element. Smullyan [1994] and note 102.
FORM 290. For all infinite x,\,|2^{x}|=|x^{x}|. Pincus [1978] and note 64.
FORM 291. For all infinite x,\,|x!|=|x^{x}|. Pincus [1978] and note 64.
FORM 292. MC(LO, \infty ): For each linearly ordered family of non-empty sets X, there is a function f such that for all x\in X\ f(x) is non-empty, finite subset of x). Howard/Rubin [1977].
FORM 293. For all sets x and y, if x can be linearly ordered and there is a mapping of x onto y, then y can be linearly ordered.
FORM 294. Every linearly ordered W-set is well orderable. Morris [1969] and note 25.
FORM 295. DO: Every infinite set has a dense linear ordering. Gonzalez [1995a].
[295 A] DUO: Every infinite set has a dense unbounded linear ordering. (An ordering is unbounded if there is neither a least element nor a greatest element.) Pincus [1997].
FORM 296. Part-\infty : Every infinite set is the disjoint union of infinitely many infinite sets. Gonzalez [1995b], Pincus [1997].
FORM 297. Extremally disconnected compact Hausdorff spaces are projective in the category of all compact Hausdorff spaces. Banaschewski [1988], Bell [1988], notes 60 and 114.
FORM 298. Every compact Hausdorff space has a Gleason cover. Bell [1988], Gleason [1958], and note 114.
FORM 299. Any extremally disconnected compact Hausdorff space is projective in the category of Boolean topological spaces. Bell [1988], notes 60 and 114.
FORM 300. Any continuous surjection between extremally disconnected compact Hausdorff spaces has an irreducible restriction to a closed subset of its domain. Bell [1988] and note 114.
FORM 301. Any continuous surjection between Boolean spaces has an irreducible restriction to a closed subset of its domain. Bell [1988] and note 114.
FORM 302. Any continuous surjection between compact Hausdorff spaces has an irreducible restriction to a closed subset of its domain. Bell [1988] and note 114.
FORM 303. If B is a Boolean algebra, S\subseteq B and S is closed under \wedge , then there is a \subseteq -maximal proper ideal I of B such that I \cap S=\{0\}. H. Rubin/J. Rubin [1985].
FORM 304. There does not exist a T_{2} topological space X such that every infinite subset of X contains an infinite compact subset. Brunner [1985].

FORM 305. There are 2^{\aleph _{0}} Vitali equivalence classes. (Vitali equivalence classes are equivalence classes of the real numbers under the relation x\equiv y\leftrightarrow (\exists q\in \mathbb{Q})(x-y=q).). Kanovei [1991].

FORM 306. The set of Vitali equivalence classes is linearly orderable. (Vitali equivalence classes are equivalence classes of the real numbers under the relation x\equiv y\leftrightarrow (\exists q\in \mathbb{Q})(x-y=q).). Kanovei [1991].

FORM 307. If m is the cardinality of the set of Vitali equivalence classes, then H(m)=H(2^{\aleph _{0}}), where H is Hartogs aleph function and the Vitali equivalence classes are equivalence classes of the real numbers under the relation x\equiv y\leftrightarrow (\exists q\in \mathbb{Q})(x-y=q). Kanovei [1991].
FORM 308(p). If p is a prime and if \{G_{y}:y\in Y\} is a set of finite groups, then the weak direct product \prod _{y\in Y}G_{y} has a maximal p-subgroup. Howard/Yorke [1987] and note 24.

[308 A(p)] If p is a prime and if Y is a set of non-empty, finite sets, then the weak direct product \prod _{y\in Y}S_{y} has a maximal p-subgroup. (S_{y} is the symmetric group on y.) Howard/Yorke [1987] and note 24.

[308 B(p)] If p is a prime and if Y is a set of non-empty finite sets such that (\forall y\in Y)(\gcd (|y|,p)=1), then Y has a choice function. (This is similar to form 46(K), but in 46(K) the set K is required to be finite.) Howard/Yorke [1987].

[308 C(p)] If p is a prime and if Y is a set of non-empty finite sets such that (\forall y\in Y)(|y|\equiv 1\mod p), then Y has a choice function. (This is similar to form 46(K), but in 46(K) the set K is required to be finite.) Howard/Yorke [1987].

FORM 309. The Banach-Tarski Paradox: There are three finite partitions \{P_{1},\,\ldots ,\,P_{n}\}, \{Q_{1},\ldots , Q_{r}\} and \{S_{1}, \ldots , S_{n}, T_{1}, \ldots , T_{r}\} of B^{3}=\{x\in \mathbb{R}^{3}:|x|\leq 1\} such that P_{i} is congruent to S_{i} for 1\leq i\leq n and Q_{i} is congruent to T_{i} for 1\leq i\leq r. Banach/Tarski [1924].

FORM 310. The Measure Extension Theorem: Suppose that \mathcal{A}_{0} is a subring (that is, a, b\in \mathcal{A}_{0}\rightarrow a\vee b\in \mathcal{A}_{0} and a-b\in \mathcal{A}_{0}) of a Boolean algebra \mathcal{A} and \mu is a measure on \mathcal{A}_{0} (that is, \mu : \mathcal{A}\rightarrow [0, \infty ],\, \mu (a\vee b)=\mu (a)+\mu (b) for a\wedge b=0, and \mu (0)=0.) then there is a measure on \mathcal{A} that extends \mu . Wagon [1985].

FORM 311. Abelian groups are amenable. (G is amenable if there is a finitely additive measure \mu on \mathcal{P}(G) such that \mu (G)=1 and \forall A\subseteq G,\,\forall g\in G,\,\mu (gA)=\mu (A).) Wagon [1985].

FORM 312. A subgroup of an amenable group is amenable. (G is amenable if there is a finitely additive measure \mu on \mathcal{P}(G) such that \mu (G)=1 and \forall A\subseteq G,\,\forall g\in G,\,\mu (gA)=\mu (A).) Wagon [1985].

FORM 313. \mathbb{Z} (the set of integers under addition) is amenable. (G is amenable if there is a finitely additive measure \mu on \mathcal{P}(G) such that \mu (G)=1 and \forall A\subseteq G,\,\forall g\in G,\,\mu (gA)=\mu (A).) Wagon [1985].
FORM 314. Every permutation on a non-empty set can be expressed as a product of two reflections. (A reflection is a permutation \phi such that \phi ^{2} is the identity.) Degen [1988].

FORM 315. \Omega =\omega _{1}, where \Omega =\{\alpha \in On: (\forall \beta \leq \alpha )(\beta =0\vee (\exists \gamma )(\beta =\gamma +1)\vee there is a sequence \langle \gamma _{n}: n\in \omega \rangle such that for each n\ \gamma _{n}<\beta and \beta =\bigcup _{n<\omega }\gamma _{n}} Gitik [1980].

FORM 316. If a linearly ordered set (A, \leq ) has the fixed point property then (A, \leq ) is complete. ((A, \leq ) has the fixed point property if every function f:A\rightarrow A satisfying (x\leq y\Rightarrow f(x)\leq f(y)) has a fixed point, and ((A, \leq ) is complete if every subset of A has a least upper bound.) Höft/Howard [1994].

FORM 317. Weak Sikorski Theorem: If B is a complete, well orderable Boolean algebra and f is a homomorphism of the Boolean algebra A^{\prime } into B where A^{\prime } is a subalgebra of the Boolean algebra A, then f can be extended to a homomorphism of A into B. Howard [1973].

[317 A] If B is a complete, well orderable Boolean algebra and A is a Boolean algebra of which B is a subalgebra, then there is an ideal I of A satisfying I\cap B =\{0\} and I is maximal among those ideals J of A satisfying J\cap B =\{0\}. Howard [1973].
FORM 318. \aleph _{1} is not measurable. Jech [1972] and note 20.
FORM 319. Measurable cardinals are inaccessible. Drake [1974] and note 20.
FORM 320. No successor cardinal, \aleph _{\alpha +1}, is measurable. Drake [1974] and note 20.
FORM 321. There does not exist an ordinal \alpha such that \aleph _{\alpha } is weakly compact and \aleph _{\alpha +1} is measurable. Bull [1978] and note 20.

FORM 322. KW(WO, \infty ), The Kinna-Wagner Selection Principle for a well ordered family of sets: For every well ordered set X there is a function f such that for all A\in M, if |A|>1 then \emptyset \neq f(A)\subsetneq A. (See form 15). Kinna/Wagner [1955], Brunner [1982a].

FORM 323. KW(\infty , WO), The Kinna-Wagner Selection Principle for a family of well orderable sets: For every set X of well orderable sets there is a function f such that for all A\in X, if |A|>1 then \emptyset \neq f(A)\subsetneq A. (See form 15.) Howard/A. Rubin/J. Rubin [1997].

FORM 324. KW(WO, WO), The Kinna-Wagner Selection Principle for a well ordered family of well orderable sets: For every well ordered set X of well orderable sets, there is a function f such that for all A\in X, if |A|>1 then \emptyset \neq f(A)\subsetneq A. (See form 15.) Howard/A. Rubin/J. Rubin [1997].

FORM 325. Ramsey’s Theorem II: \forall n,\,m\in \omega , if A is an infinite set and the family of all m element subsets of A is partitioned into n sets S_{j},\,1\leq j\leq n, then there is an infinite subset B\subseteq A such that all m element subsets of B belong to the same S_{j}. (Also, see form 17.) Ramsey [1929].

FORM 326. 2-SAT: Restricted Compactness Theorem for Propositional Logic III: If \Sigma is a set of formulas in a propositional language such that every finite subset of \Sigma is satisfiable and if every formula in \Sigma is a disjunction of at most two literals, then \Sigma is satisfiable. (A literal is a propositional variable or its negation.) Wojtylak [1995].

FORM 327. KW(WO, <\aleph _{0}), The Kinna-Wagner Selection Principle for a well ordered family of finite sets: For every well ordered set X of finite sets there is a function f such that for all A\in X, if |A|>1 then \emptyset \neq f(A)\subsetneq A. (See form 15.) Howard/A. Rubin/J. Rubin [1997].

FORM 328. MC(WO, \infty ): For every well ordered set X such that for all x\in X,\,|x|\geq 1, there is a function f such that and for every x\in X,\,f(x) is a finite, non-empty subset of x. (See form 67.) Howard/A. Rubin/J. Rubin [1997].

FORM 329. MC(\infty , WO): For every set M of well orderable sets such that for all x\in X,\,|x|\geq 1, there is a function f such that for every x\in X,\,f(x) is a finite, non-empty subset of x. (See form 67.) Howard/A. Rubin/J. Rubin [1997].

FORM 330. MC(WO, WO): For every well ordered set X of well orderable sets such that for all x\in X,\, |x|\geq 1, there is a function f such that for every x\in X,\,f(x) is a finite, non-empty subset of x. (See form 67.) Howard/A. Rubin/J. Rubin [1997].

FORM 331. If (X_{i})_{i\in I} is a family of compact non-empty topological spaces then there is a family (F_{i})_{i\in I} such that \forall i\in I,\,F_{i} is an irreducible closed subset of X_{i}. Morillon [1988] and note 71.
FORM 332. A product of non-empty compact sober topological spaces is nonempty. Morillon [1988] and note 71.

FORM 333. MC(\infty , \infty , \mathrm{odd}): For every set X of sets such that for all x\in X,\,|x|\geq 1, there is a function f such that for every x\in X,\,f(x) is a finite, non-empty subset of x and |f(x)| is odd. Keremedis [1996a].
[333 A] In every vector space B over the two element field, every subspace of B has a complementary subspace. Keremedis [1996a].
[333 B] Every quotient group of an Abelian group each of whose non-unit elements has order 2 has a set of representatives. Keremedis [1996a].

FORM 334. MC(\infty , \infty , \mathrm{even}): For every set X of sets such that for all x\in X,\,|x|\geq 2, there is a function f such that for every x\in X,\,f(x) is a finite, non-empty subset of x and |f(x)| is even. Keremedis [1996a].
FORM 335(n). Every quotient group of an Abelian group each of whose elements has order \leq n has a set of representatives. Keremedis [1996].
FORM 336(n). (For n\in \omega ,\,n\geq 2.) For every infinite set X, there is an infinite Y\subseteq X such that the set of all n-element subsets of Y has a choice function. Note 111.
FORM 337. Every separable metric space is Lindelöf. Good/Tree [1995].
FORM 338. Every second countable metric space is Lindelöf. Good/Tree [1995].
FORM 339. Every second countable metric space is separable. Good/Tree [1995].
FORM 340. Every Lindelöf metric space is separable. Good/Tree [1995].
FORM 341. Every Lindelöf metric space is second countable. Good/Tree [1995].
FORM 342(n). (For n\in \omega , n\geq 2.)\ PC(\infty , n, \infty ): Every infinite family of n-element sets has an infinite subfamily with a choice function. (See form 166.) Note 111.
FORM 343. A product of non-empty, compact T_{2} topological spaces is non-empty. Morillon [1988].
FORM 344. If (E_{i})_{i\in I} is a family of non-empty sets, then there is a family (U_{i})_{i\in I} such that \forall i\in I,\,U_{i} is an ultrafilter on E_{i}. Morillon [1988].

FORM 345. Rasiowa-Sikorski Axiom: If (B, \wedge , \vee ) is a Boolean algebra, a is a non-zero element of B, and \{X_{n}:n\in \omega \} is a denumerable set of subsets of B then there is a maximal prime filter F of B such that a\in F and for each n\in \omega , if X_{n}\subseteq F and \bigwedge X_{n} exists then \bigwedge X_{n}\in F. Morillon [1988].
[345 A] Form 14 + form 43. Morillon [1988].
[345 B] Form 14 + form 106. Morillon [1988].
[345 C] Every bounded, distributive lattice has the strong Rasiowa-Sikorski property. Morillon [1988] and note 71.
[345 D] Every bounded, distributive lattice has the Rasiowa-Sikorski property. Morillon [1988] and note 71.
[345 E] Every Boolean algebra has the Rasiowa-Sikorski property. Morillon [1988] and note 71.

FORM 346. Vector Space Kinna-Wagner Principle: For every family V=\{V_{i}:i\in K\} of non-trivial vector spaces there is a family F=\{F_{i}:i\in K\} such that for each i\in K,\,F_{i} is a non-empty, independent subset of V_{i}. Note 127.
FORM 347. Idemmultiple Partition Principle: If y is idemmultiple (2\times y\approx y) and x\precsim ^{\ast } y, then x\precsim y. Higasikawa [1995] and note 69.
FORM 348. If G is a group and X and Y both freely generate G then |X|=|Y|. Federer/Jonsson [1950] and Howard [1985].
FORM 349. MC(\infty , \aleph _{0}): For every set X of non-empty denumerable sets there is a function f such that for all x\in X,\,f(x) is a finite, non-empty subset of x.

FORM 350. MC(\aleph _{0}, \aleph _{0}): For every denumerable set X of non-empty denumerable sets there is a function f such that for all x\in X,\,f(x) is a finite, non-empty subset of x. Keremedis [1996] and note 132.
FORM 351. A countable product of metrizable spaces is metrizable. Keremedis [1996] and note 132.
FORM 352. A countable product of second countable spaces is second countable. Keremedis [1996] and note 132.
FORM 353. A countable product of first countable spaces is first countable. Keremedis [1996] and note 132.
FORM 354. A countable product of separable T_{2} spaces is separable. Keremedis [1996] and note 132.

FORM 355. KW(\aleph _{0}, \infty ), The Kinna-Wagner Selection Principle for a denumerable family of sets: For every denumerable set X there is a function f such that for all A\in X, if |A|>1 then \emptyset \neq f(A)\subsetneq A.

FORM 356. KW(\infty , \aleph _{0}), The Kinna-Wagner Selection Principle for a family of denumerable sets: For every set X of denumerable sets there is a function f such that for all A\in X, if |A|>1 then \emptyset \neq f(A)\subsetneq A.

FORM 357. KW(\aleph _{0}, \aleph _{0}), The Kinna-Wagner Selection Principle for a denumerable family of denumerable sets: For every denumerable set X of denumerable sets there is a function f such that for all A\in X, if |A|>1 then \emptyset \neq f(A)\subsetneq A.

FORM 358. KW(\aleph _{0}, <\aleph _{0}), The Kinna-Wagner Selection Principle for a denumerable family of finite sets: For every denumerable set X of finite sets there is a function f such that for all A\in X, if |A|>1 then \emptyset \neq f(A)\subsetneq A.

FORM 359. If \{A_{x}:x\in S\} and \{B_{x}:x\in S\} are families of pairwise disjoint sets and |A_{x}|\leq |B_{x}| for all x\in S, then |\bigcup _{x\in S}A_{x}|\leq |\bigcup _{x\in S}B_{x}|. Higasikawa [1995].
FORM 360. Every second countable topological space is Lindelöf. G. Moore [1982] p 236.
FORM 361. In \mathbb{R}, the union of a denumerable number of analytic sets is analytic. G. Moore [1982], pp 181 and 325.
FORM 362. In \mathbb{R}, every Borel set is analytic. G. Moore [1982], pp 181 and 325.
FORM 363. There are exactly 2^{\aleph _{0}} Borel sets in \mathbb{R}. G. Moore [1982], p 325.
FORM 364. In \mathbb{R}, there is a measurable set that is not Borel. G. Moore [1982], p 325.
FORM 365. For every uncountable set A, if A has the same cardinality as each of its uncountable subsets then |A|=\aleph _{1}. Sierpiński [1918].
FORM 366. There is a discontinuous function f:\mathbb{R} \rightarrow \mathbb{R} such that for all real x and y,\,f(x+y)=f(x)+f(y). Hamel [1905].
FORM 367. There is a Hamel basis for \mathbb{R} as a vector space over \mathbb{Q}. Hamel [1905].
FORM 368. The set of all denumerable subsets of \mathbb{R} has power 2^{\aleph _{0}}. Sierpiński [1917].
FORM 369. If \mathbb{R} is partitioned into two sets, at least one of them has cardinality 2^{\aleph _{0}}. Luzin/Sierpiński [1917].
FORM 370. Weak Gelfand Extreme Point Theorem: If A is a non-trivial Gelfand algebra then the closed unit ball in the dual of A has an extreme point e. Morillon [1986], notes 23 and 29.

[370 A] Measured Boolean Prime Ideal Theorem: If \mathcal{B} is a Boolean algebra and there is a measure on \mathcal{B} then there is an ultrafilter on \mathcal{B}. Morillon [1989], [1990] and note 147.
FORM 371. There is an infinite, compact, Hausdorff, extremally disconnected topological space. Morillon [1993] and note 114.

FORM 372. Generalized Hahn-Banach Theorem: Assume that X is a real vector space, (Z,\preccurlyeq ) is a Dedekind complete ordered vector space and X_{0} is a subspace of X. If \lambda _{0}:X_{0}\rightarrow Z is linear and p:X\rightarrow Z is sublinear and if \lambda _{0}\preccurlyeq p on X_{0} then \lambda _{0} can be extended to a linear map \lambda :X\rightarrow Z such that \lambda \preccurlyeq p on X. Schechter [1996b] and note 31.

[372 A] Existence of Banach Limits: For any directed set (\Delta , \sqsubseteq ) and any Dedekind complete ordered vector space (Z,\preccurlyeq ) there exists a Z-valued Banach limit. Schechter [1996b] and note 31.

[372 B] Generalized Convex Domination Theorem: For every real vector space X, every Dedekind complete ordered vector space (Z, \preccurlyeq ), every subspace X_{0}\subseteq X, every linear \lambda _{0}:X_{0}\rightarrow Z and every convex p:X\rightarrow Z, if \lambda _{0}\preccurlyeq p on X_{0} then \lambda _{0} can be extended to a linear map \lambda :X\rightarrow Z such that \lambda \preccurlyeq p on X. Schechter [1996b] and note 31.

[372 C] Generalized Support Theorem: For every real vector space X and every Dedekind complete ordered vector space (Z, \preccurlyeq ), every convex function p:X\rightarrow Z is a pointwise maximum of affine functions. Schechter [1996b] and note 31.

[372 D] Generalized Sandwich Theorem: For every real vector space X and every Dedekind complete ordered vector space (Z,\preccurlyeq ), if e:X\rightarrow Z is a concave function, g:X\rightarrow Z is a convex function, and e\leq g everywhere on X, then there exists an affine function f:X\rightarrow Z satisfying e\leq f\leq g everywhere on X. Schechter [1996b] and note 31.
FORM 373(n). (For n\in w, n\geq 2.) PC(\aleph _{0}, n, \infty ): Every denumerable set of n-element sets has an infinite subset with a choice function.
[373 A(n)] (For n\in \omega , n\geq 2.)\ PC(WO, n, \infty ): Every infinite well ordered set of n-element sets has an infinite subset with a choice function.
[373 B(n)] PUT(\aleph _{0}, n, \aleph _{0}) for n\in \omega -\{0,1\}: The union of a denumerable set of pairwise disjoint n-element sets has a denumerable subset.
[373 C(n)] PUT(WO, n, WO) for n\in w-\{0, 1\}: The union of an infinite well ordered set of pairwise disjoint n-element sets has an infinite well ordered subset.
FORM 374(n). UT(\aleph _{0}, n, \aleph _{0}) for n\in \omega -\{0,1\}: The union of a denumerable set of n-element sets is denumerable.
[374 A(n)] For each i,\,2\leq i\leq n\in \omega -\{0,1\}, C(\aleph _{0}, i): Every denumerable set of i-element sets has a choice function.

FORM 375. Tietze-Urysohn Extension Theorem: If (X, T) is a normal topological space, A is closed in X, and f:A\rightarrow [0,1] is continuous, then there exists a continuous function g:X\rightarrow [0, 1] which extends f. Urysohn [1924].

FORM 376. Restricted Kinna Wagner Principle: For every infinite set X there is an infinite subset Y of X and a function f such that for every z\subseteq Y, if |z|\geq 2 then f(z) is a non-empty proper subset of z. De la Cruz/Di Prisco [1996].
FORM 377. Restricted Ordering Principle: For every infinite set X there is an infinite subset Y of X such that Y can be linearly ordered. De la Cruz/Di Prisco [1996].

FORM 378. Restricted Choice for Families of Well Ordered Sets: For every infinite set X there is an infinite subset Y of X such that the family of non-empty well orderable subsets of Y has a choice function. De la Cruz/Di Prisco [1996].

[378A] Restricted Choice for Families of Finite Sets: For every infinite set X there is an infinite subset Y of X such that the family of non-empty Finite subsets of Y has a choice function. De la Cruz/Di Prisco [1996].

FORM 379. PKW(\infty , \infty , \infty ): For every infinite family X of sets each of which has at least two elements, there is an infinite subfamily Y of X and a function f such that for all y\in Y,\, f(y) is a non-empty proper subset of y. De la Cruz/Di Prisco [1996].
FORM 380. PC(\infty , WO, \infty ): For every infinite family of non-empty well orderable sets, there is an infinite subfamily Y of X which has a choice function. De la Cruz/Di Prisco [1996].
FORM 381. DUM: The disjoint union of metrizable spaces is metrizable. Howard/Keremedis/Rubin/Rubin [1997b].
FORM 382. DUMN: The disjoint union of metrizable spaces is normal. Howard/Keremedis/Rubin/Rubin [1997b].
FORM 383. MP: Every metric space is paracompact. Howard/Keremedis/Rubin/Stanley [1997] and note 141.

[383 A] Every open cover \mathcal{U} of a metric space (X, d) has a refinement \mathcal{V} which covers X and which can be written as a well ordered union \bigcup \{V_{\alpha }:\alpha \in \gamma \} where each V_{\alpha } is locally finite. Howard/Keremedis/Rubin/Stanley [1997] and note 141.
[383 B] MM: Every metric space is metacompact. Howard/Keremedis/Rubin/Stanley [1997] and note 141.

[383 C] Every open cover \mathcal{U} of a metric space (X, d) has a refinement \mathcal{V} which covers X and which can be written as a well ordered union \bigcup \{V_{\alpha }:\alpha \in \gamma \} where each V_{\alpha } is point finite. Howard/Keremedis/Rubin/Stanley [1997] and note 141.

sec.title: ALGEBRAIC FORMS
sec.p: [1 BA] (Depends on the prime p) Every group has a maximal p-subgroup. Howard/Yorke [1987] and note 24.

[1 BB] Strong Nielsen-Schreier Theorem II: If G is a group which is freely generated by X and U is a subgroup of G, then there is a subset A of G which freely generates U and is level with respect to X. Howard [1985] and note 129.
[1 BS] For every Abelian group (G,\,+), for every H\subseteq G, the infinite system of equations
has a solution in H iff each of its equations has a solution in H. Keremedis [1996c].
[1 BX] For every Abelian group G and every subgroup H of G there exists a set of representatives for the quotient G/H. Keremedis [1996c].

[1 CA] Strong Nielsen-Schreier Theorem I: If G is a group which is freely generated by X and U is a subgroup of G, then there is a subset A of G which freely generates U and has the Nielsen property with respect to X. Howard [1985] and note 129.
[62 A] (Depends on the two primes p_{1}\neq p_{2}) Form 308(p_{1})+ form 308(p_{2}). Howard/Yorke [1987].
[62 B] (Depends on the prime p_{1}) Form 45(p_{1})+ form 308(p_{1}). Howard/Yorke [1987].
[62 C] For every prime p, if \{G_{y}:y\in Y\} is a set of finite groups, then the weak direct product \prod _{y\in Y}G_{y} has a maximal p-subgroup. Howard/Yorke [1987] and note 24.

[62 D] For every prime p, if Y is a set of non-empty, finite sets, then the weak direct product \prod _{y\in Y}S_{y} has a maximal p-subgroup. (S_{y} is the symmetric group on y.) Howard/Yorke [1987] and note 24.
[67 D] For every Abelian group A, every torsion free divisible subgroup of A is a direct summand of A. Armbrust [1972] and note 24.
68. Nielsen-Schreier Theorem: Every subgroup of a free group is free. Jech [1973b] p12.
176. Every infinite, locally finite group has an infinite Abelian subgroup. (Locally finite means every finite subset generates a finite subgroup.) Plotkin [1981].

180. Every Abelian group has a divisible hull. (If A and B are groups, B is a divisible hull of A means B is a divisible group, A is a subgroup of B and for every non-zero b\in B,\,\exists n\in w such that 0\neq nb\in A.) Fuchs [1970], Theorem 24.4 p 107, Hodges [1980], and note 24.
188. EP Ab: For every Abelian group A there is a projective Abelian group G and a homomorphism from G onto A. Blass [1979] and note 60.
189. EI Ab: For every Abelian group A there is an injective Abelian group G and a one to one homomorphism from A into G. Blass [1979] and note 60.
190. There is a non-trivial injective Abelian group. Blass [1979] and note 60.
193. EFP Ab: Every Abelian group is a homomorphic image of a free projective Abelian group. Blass [1979] and note 60.
210. The commutator subgroup of a free group is free. Läuchli [1962].
220(p). Suppose p\in \omega and p is a prime. Any two elementary Abelian p-groups (all non-trivial elements have order p) of the same cardinality are isomorphic. Hickman [1977b].
227. For all groups G, if every finite subgroup of G can be fully ordered then G can be fully ordered. Rav [1977] and note 79.
228. Every torsion free Abelian group can be fully ordered. Rav [1977] and note 79.

229. If (G,\,\circ ,\,\leq ) is a partially ordered group, then \leq can be extended to a linear order on G if and only if for every finite set \{a_{1},\,\ldots ,\,a_{n}\}\subseteq G, with a_{i}\neq the identity for i=1 to n, the signs \epsilon _{1},\,\ldots ,\,\epsilon _{n}\,(\epsilon _{i}=\pm 1) can be chosen so that P\cap S(a_{1}^{\epsilon _{1}},\,\ldots ,\,a_{n}^{\epsilon _{n}})=\emptyset (where S(b_{1},\, \ldots ,\,b_{n}) is the normal sub-semi-group of G generated by b_{1},\,\ldots ,\,b_{n} and P=\{g\in G:e\leq g\} where e is the identity of G.) Rav [1977].
237. The order of any group is divisible by the order of any of its subgroups, (i.e., if H is a subgroup of G then there is a set A such that |H\times A|=|G|.) Hickman [1976].
238. Every elementary Abelian group (that is, for some prime p every non identity element has order p) is the direct sum of cyclic subgroups. Hickman [1976].
239. For all X, if X\neq \emptyset , then there is a binary operation on X that makes X a group. Hickman [1976].
240. If a group G satisfies “every ascending chain of subgroups is finite,” then every subgroup of G is finitely generated. Hickman [1976].
251. The additive groups (\mathbb{R},\,+) and (\mathbb{C},\,+) are isomorphic. Ash [1975].
252. The additive groups of \mathbb{Q} \oplus \mathbb{R} and \mathbb{R} are isomorphic. Ash [1975].
308(p). If p is a prime and if \{G_{y}:y\in Y\} is a set of finite groups, then the weak direct product \prod _{y\in Y}G_{y} has a maximal p-subgroup. Howard/Yorke [1987] and note 24.

[308A(p)] If p is a prime and if Y is a set of non-empty, finite sets, then the weak direct product \prod _{y\in Y}S_{y} has a maximal p-subgroup (S_{y} is the symmetric group on y.) Howard/Yorke [1987] and note 24.

311. Abelian groups are amenable. (G is amenable if there is a finitely additive measure \mu on \mathcal{P}(G) such that \mu (G)=1 and \forall A\subseteq G,\,\forall g\in G,\,\mu (gA)=\mu (A).) Wagon [1985].

312. A subgroup of an amenable group is amenable. (G is amenable if there is a finitely additive measure \mu on \mathcal{P}(G) such that \mu (G)=1 and \forall A\subseteq G,\,\forall g\in G,\,\mu (gA)=\mu (A).) Wagon [1985].

313. \mathbb{Z} (the set of integers under addition) is amenable. (G is amenable if there is a finitely additive measure \mu on \mathcal{P}(G) such that \mu (G)=1 and \forall A\subseteq G,\,\forall g\in G,\,\mu (gA)=\mu (A).) Wagon [1985].
314. Every permutation on a non-empty set can be expressed as a product of two reflections. (A reflection is a permutation \phi such that \phi ^{2} is the identity.) Degen [1988].
[333 B] Every quotient group of an Abelian group each of whose non-unit elements has order 2 has a set of representatives. Keremedis [1996a].
335 (n). Every quotient group of an Abelian group each of whose elements has order \leq n has a set of representatives. Keremedis [1996c].
348. If G is a group and X and Y both freely generate G then |X|=|Y|. Federer/Jonsson [1950] and Howard [1985].

[1 AN] Every lattice \langle L, \cap ,\,\cup , \subseteq \rangle of sets (that is, L is a family of sets and \cap ,\,\cup and \subseteq are the usual operations) with a greatest element has a maximal, proper ideal. Bell/Fremlin [1972].

[14 E] Almost Maximal Ideal Theorem: Every bounded, non-trivial, distributive lattice has an almost maximal ideal. (Definitions: If D is a bounded non-trivial distributive lattice, I(D) is the lattice of ideals of D. An almost maximal ideal in D is an ideal P of D such that s(P)=P where s is the operation on I(D) defined as follows: If e is the unit of I(D), (i) For a\in I(D) we say x\in I(D) is a-small if x\vee b=e implies a\vee b=e for all b\in I(D). (ii) For any a\in I(D), s(a) is the join of all a-small elements of I(D)). Banaschewski/Harting [1985] and Blass [1986].
[14 F] Every non-trivial complete distributive lattice with compact unit has a prime ideal. Banaschewski [1985] and note 29.
[14 R] Every coherent local lattice is spatial. Banaschewski [1981] and note 29.
[14 S] Every compact, regular local lattice is spatial. Banaschewski [1981] and note 29.
[14 AE] For any distributive lattice D with zero and unit, any ideal J\subseteq D and a\not \in J, there is a prime filter F such that a\in F and F\cap J=\emptyset . Banaschewski [1981].

[14 AU] If Z is a real vector lattice with order unit 1 then the set of all positive linear functionals u on Z with u(1)=1 is a convex set that has an extreme point. See H. Rubin/J. Rubin [1985], pages 177 and 182 for definitions. Also see Gardiner [1974].
[14 BH] The sum of finite frames is a spatial frame. Paseka [1989] and note 29.
[14 BI] Every compact, conjunctive frame is spatial. Paseka [1989] and note 29.
[14 BJ] The sum of compact, regular frames is spatial. Paseka [1989] and note 29.
[14 BL] Every compact, 0 dimensional frame is spatial. Paseka [1989] and note 29.
[14 BP] Every non-empty bounded distributive lattice has a prime ideal. Morillon [1988].
[14 BQ] Every proper ideal in a bounded distributive lattice is the intersection of the prime ideals containing it. Morillon [1988] and note 79. (Compare with [14 AE]).
[14 BR] Every \vee -compact non trivial lattice has a principal prime ideal. Morillon [1988], [1985] and note 71.
[14 BS] Every bounded distributive lattice has a prime ideal choice function. Morillon [1988], [1985] and note 71.

[14 BT] If (A_{i})_{i\in I} is a family of bounded, distributive, \vee -compact lattices and if (J_{i})_{i\in I} is a family such that for all i\in I,\,J_{i} is a proper ideal in A_{i} then there is a family (P_{i})_{i\in I} such that for all i\in I,\,P_{i} is a prime principal ideal in A_{i} containing J_{i}. Morillon [1985], [1988] and note 71.

[14 BU] If (A_{i})_{i\in I} is a family of distributive non trivial bounded lattices, then there is a family (f_{i})_{i\in I} such that each f_{i} is a prime ideal choice function on A_{i}. Morillon [1985], [1988] and note 71.

[14 CH] For every bounded, distributive lattice (A, \wedge , \vee ) in which 0 is \wedge -compact, for all a\in A,\,a\neq 0 and for all sequences (X_{n})_{n\in \omega } of subsets of A, there is a prime filter in A which contains a and respects each X_{n}. Morillon [1988] and note 71.
[50 C] Every DeMorgan compact regular frame is injective in the category of all such frames. Banaschewski [1988], notes 29 and 60.

[50 D] For any extension M\supseteq L of a compact regular frame L, there is an s\in M maximal with respect to the property that x\vee s=1\rightarrow x=1 for all x\in L. Banaschewski [1988], notes 29 and 60.
[86 B(\alpha )] The frame envelope of any \aleph _{\alpha } frame is \aleph _{\alpha }-Lindelöf. Banaschewski [1997] and note 29.

[88 C] If m is a cardinal number and \mathcal{L} is a lattice isomorphic to the lattice of subalgebras of some unary universal algebra (a unary universal algebra is one with only unary or nullary operations) and \alpha is an automorphism of \mathcal{L} of order 2 (that is, \alpha ^{2} is the identity) then there is a unary algebra \mathfrak{A} with |\ \mathrm{domain}\ \mathfrak{A}|\geq m and an isomorphism \rho from \mathcal{L} onto the lattice of subalgebras of \mathfrak{A}^{2} with \rho (\alpha (x))=(\rho (x))^{-1}(=\{(s,\,t):(t,\,s)\in \rho (x)\}) for all x\in \mathcal{L}. Lampe [1974].

268. If \mathcal{L} is a lattice isomorphic to the lattice of subalgebras of some unary universal algebra (a unary universal algebra is one with only unary or nullary operations) and \alpha is an automorphism of \mathcal{L} of order 2 (that is, \alpha ^{2} is the identity) then there is a unary algebra \mathfrak{A} and an isomorphism \rho from \mathcal{L} onto the lattice of subalgebras of \mathfrak{A}^{2} with \rho (\alpha (x))=(\rho (x))^{-1}(=\{(s,\,t):(t,\,s)\in \rho (x)\}) for all x\in \mathcal{L}. Lampe [1974].
[345 C] Every bounded, distributive lattice has the strong Rasiowa-Sikorski property. Morillon [1988] and note 71.
[345 D] Every bounded, distributive lattice has the Rasiowa-Sikorski property. Morillon [1988] and note 71.
[\boldsymbol{0} Y] There is no free complete Boolean algebra over D if |D|\geq \aleph _{0}. Stavi [1975], Gaifman [1970], Hales [1964], and note 89.
[1 BT] For every Boolean ring (B,\,+,\,\cdot ) and every H\subseteq B which is closed under + there exists a \subseteq -maximal ideal Q\subseteq B such that H\cap Q=\{0\}. Keremedis [1996c].
14. BPI: Every Boolean algebra has a prime ideal. M. Stone [1936].
[14 B] Stone Representation Theorem: Every Boolean algebra is isomorphic to a set algebra. Jech [1973b] p 27 prob 2.12 and M. Stone [1936].
[14 AV] Every Boolean algebra has a 2-valued measure. Pincus [1972c] and note 147.

[14 BA] Monteiro’s Theorem for Complete Atomic Boolean Algebras: Let K be a complete atomic Boolean algebra, A a subalgebra of the Boolean algebra B and f a homomorphism from A to K. Let d be a semimorphism from B into K (that is, d\,:\,B\rightarrow K,\,d(0)=0,\,d(1)=1 and for all x,\,y\in B,\, d(x\vee y)=d(x)\vee d(y) ) with f(x)\leq d(x) for all x\in A. Then there is a homomorphism h from B to K such that h(x)\leq d(x) for all x\in B and h/A=f. Monteiro [1965] and Bacsich [1972].

[14 BC] If m_{0} is an additive, real valued measure on a subalgebra \mathcal{B}_{0} of a Boolean algebra \mathcal{B} then there exists a measure m on \mathcal{B} such that m=m_{0} on \mathcal{B}_{0} and the range of m is contained in the closure of the range of m_{0}. Tarski [1930] and note 147.
[14 BK] The sum of 4-element Boolean algebras is spatial. Paseka [1989] and note 29.

[43 A] Tarski’s Lemma: Let \{x(n):n\in \omega \} be a denumerable collection of subsets of a Boolean algebra B each of which has a meet in B. Then for any a\neq 0 in B there is a proper filter F of B that decides \bigwedge x(n) for all n and has a\in F. (F decides \bigwedge x(n) if either \bigwedge x(n)\in F or t\not \in F for some t\in x(n).) Goldblatt [1985].

50. Sikorski’s Extension Theorem: Every homomorphism of a subalgebra B of a Boolean algebra A into a complete Boolean algebra B^{\prime } can be extended to a homomorphism of A into B^{\prime }. Sikorski [1964], p 141.
[50 A] Every complete Boolean algebra is injective. Banaschewski [1988].

[50 B] Monteiro’s Theorem: Let K be a complete Boolean algebra, A a subalgebra of the Boolean algebra B and f a homomorphism from A to K. Let d be a semimorphism from B into K (that is, d:B\rightarrow K,\,d(0)=0,\,d(1)=1 and for all x and y in B,\,d(x\vee y)=d(x)\vee d(y)) with f(x)\leq d(x) for all x\in A. Then there is a homomorphism h from B to K such that h(x)\leq d(x) for all x\in B and h/A=f. Monteiro [1965] and Bacsich [1972].
[50 E] Form 14 + form 297. Banaschewski [1988] and Bell [1988].

[50 F] For any complete Boolean algebra B and any subalgebra A of B, there is a U\in V^{(B)} such that V^{(B)}\models \ {``} U is an ultrafilter on A and U^{B}\subseteq U”. (V^{(B)} is the Boolean valued universe constructed from B,\,U^{B}=\{(\hat{x},\,x):x\in B\} is the canonical ultrafilter on B and x\mapsto \hat{x} is the canonical embedding of V into V^{(B)}.) Bell [1977] and [1983].

[50 G] For any complete Boolean algebra B and any C\in V^{(B)} such that V^{(B)}\models {``}C is a Boolean algebra.” there is a U\in V^{(B)} such that V^{(B)}\models {``}U is an ultrafilter in C.” See [50 F] for definitions. Bell [1983].

[50 H] If m:A\rightarrow B is a monomorphism between Boolean algebras, then there is an m-minimal epimorphism p:B\rightarrow C to some Boolean algebra C. (p is m-minimal if (1) p\circ m is monic and (2) if q:C\rightarrow D is any epimorphism to a Boolean algebra D such that q\circ p\circ m is monic, then q is an isomorphism.) Bell [1988].
[50 I] If A is a subalgebra of a Boolean algebra B, then there is a \subseteq -maximal proper filter F in B such that F\cap A=\{1\}. Bell [1988]
[50 J] Form 299+ form 14. Bell [1988].
[50 K] Form 300+ form 14. Bell [1988].
[50 L] Form 301+ form 14. Bell [1988].
[50 M] Form 302+ form 14. Bell [1988].
[52 A] On every Boolean algebra there is an additive real valued measure. Luxemburg [1969] and note 147.

[52 B] For every proper filter \mathcal{F} of elements of a Boolean algebra \mathcal{B}, there exists an additive, real valued measure m on \mathcal{B} such that m(x)=1 for all x\in \mathcal{F}. Luxemburg [1969] and note 147.

[52 C] For every non-empty set X and every proper ideal \mathcal{I} of in \mathcal{P}(X) there is a measure m on \mathcal{P}(X) such that m(x)=0 for all x\in \mathcal{I}. Luxemburg [1969] and note 147.

[52 D] Let \mathcal{B}_{0} be a subalgebra of a Boolean algebra \mathcal{B} and m_{0} an additive, real valued measure on \mathcal{B}_{0}. Then there is a real valued, additive measure m on \mathcal{B} such that m=m_{0} on \mathcal{B}_{0} and the range of m is contained in the closed convex hull of the range of m_{0}. Luxemburg [1969] and note 147.
[123 A] Form 70+ form 344. Morillon [1988].
201. Linking Axiom for Boolean Algebras: Every Boolean algebra has a maximal linked system. (L\subseteq B is linked if a\wedge b\neq 0 for all a and b\in L.) Schrijver [1978].

[201 A] Strong Linking Axiom for Boolean Algebras: Each linked system in a Boolean algebra is contained in some maximal linked system. (If B is a Boolean algebra, L\subseteq B is linked if a\wedge b\neq 0 for all a and b\in L.) Schrijver [1978].
247. Every atomless Boolean algebra is Dedekind infinite. Plotkin [1976], notes 86 and 94.
248. For any \kappa ,\,\kappa is the cardinal number of an infinite complete Boolean algebra if and only if \kappa ^{\aleph _{0}}=\kappa . Plotkin [1976] and note 86.
267. There is no infinite, free complete Boolean algebra. Stavi [1975] and note 89.
303. If B is a Boolean algebra, S\subseteq B and S is closed under \wedge , then there is a \subseteq -maximal proper ideal I of B such that I \cap S=\{0\}. H. Rubin/J. Rubin [1985].

310. The Measure Extension Theorem: Suppose that \mathcal{A}_{0} is a subring (that is, a,\,b\in \mathcal{A}_{0}\rightarrow a\vee b\in \mathcal{A}_{0} and a-b\in \mathcal{A}_{0}) of a Boolean algebra \mathcal{A} and \mu is a measure on \mathcal{A}_{0} (that is, \mu \,:\,\mathcal{A}\rightarrow [0,\,\infty ],\,\mu (a\vee b)=\mu (a)+\mu (b) for a\wedge b=0, and \mu (0)=0.) then there is a measure on \mathcal{A} that extends \mu . Wagon [1985].

317. Weak Sikorski Theorem: If B is a complete, well orderable Boolean algebra and f is a homomorphism of the Boolean algebra A^{\prime } into B where A^{\prime } is a subalgebra of the Boolean algebra A, then f can be extended to a homomorphism of A into B. Howard [1973].

[317 A] If B is a complete, well orderable Boolean algebra and A is a Boolean algebra of which B is a subalgebra, then there is an ideal I of A satisfying I\cap B =\{0\} and I is maximal among those ideals J of A satisfying J\cap B=\{0\}. Howard [1973].
344. If (E_{i})_{i\in I} is a family of non-empty sets, then there is a family (U_{i})_{i\in I} such that \forall i\in I,\,U_{i} is an ultrafilter on E_{i}. Morillon [1988].

345. Rasiowa-Sikorski Axiom: If (B,\,\wedge ,\,\vee ) is a Boolean algebra, a is a non-zero element of B, and \{X_{n}:n\in w\} is a denumerable set of subsets of B then there is a maximal prime filter F of B such that a\in F and for each n\in \omega , if X_{n}\subseteq F and \bigwedge X_{n} exists then \bigwedge X_{n}\in F. Morillon [1988].
[345 A] Form 14+ form 43. Morillon [1988].
[345 B] Form 14+ form 106. Morillon [1988].
[345 E] Every Boolean algebra has the Rasiowa-Sikorski property. Morillon [1988] and note 71.

[370 A] Measured Boolean Prime Ideal Theorem: If \mathcal{B} is a Boolean algebra and there is a measure on \mathcal{B} then there is an ultrafilter on \mathcal{B}. Morillon [1989], [1990] and note 147.
B. Fields (Including Algebraic Properties of \mathbb{R} and \mathbb{Q}) (See note 45.)
[\boldsymbol{0} R] Every infinite Dedekind finite field is the direct limit of a strictly increasing \omega -sequence of finite subfields. Hickman [1982], notes 45 and 94.
[14 BN] A system of equations over a finite field F has a solution in F if and only if every finite sub-system has a solution in F. Cowen/Emerson [1995] and note 30.
69. Every field has an algebraic closure. Jech [1973b] p 13.

72. Artin-Schreier Theorem: Every field in which -1 is not the sum of squares can be ordered. (The ordering, \leq , must satisfy (a) a\leq b\rightarrow a+c\leq b+c for all c and (b) c\geq 0 and a\leq b\rightarrow a\cdot c\leq b\cdot \mathrm{c}.) Tarski [1954b].
233. If a field has an algebraic closure it is unique up to isomorphism. Mathias [1977b].
241. Every algebraic closure of \mathbb{Q} has a real closed subfield. Hodges [1976a], Läuchli [1962] and note 84.
242. There is, up to an isomorphism, at most one algebraic closure of \mathbb{Q}. Hodges [1976a], Läuchli [1962] and note 84.
284. A system of linear equations over a field F has a solution in F if and only if every finite sub-system has a solution in F. Cowen/Emerson [1995].
367. There is a Hamel basis for \mathbb{R} as a vector space over \mathbb{Q}. Hamel [1905].
[1 B] Every commutative ring with unit has a maximal ideal. Hodges [1979].
[1 CD] In a commutative ring, every proper ideal can be extended to a maximal ideal. Krull [1929]. ([1 CD] implies [1 B]).
[14 C] Every commutative ring with unit has a prime ideal. Scott [1954].

[14 D] Every ring with unit has a (two sided) prime ideal. (An ideal P in a ring R is prime if P\neq R and for any ideals A and B in R, if AB\subseteq P then A\subseteq P or B\subseteq P.) Blass [1986] and Banaschewski [1985].
[14 T] Every regular commutative ring with unit has a maximal ideal. Banaschewski [1983] and note 29.
[14 U] Every closed proper ideal in a Gelfand algebra is contained in some maximal ideal. Banaschewski [1983] and note 29.

[14 AL] The radical of a proper ideal A in a commutative ring R with identity is the intersection of all prime ideals in R containing A. (The radical of A= \{x\in R:\ {for some}\ m\in \omega ,\, x^{m}\in A\}.) Rav [1977] and note 80.
[14 AM] Let A be a subring of a commutative ring R and p a prime ideal in A such that p=Rp\cap A. Then there is a prime ideal J in R such that p=J\cap A. Rav [1977] and note 80.
[14 AN] In every commutative ring with identity, every proper ideal is included in some prime ideal. Rav [1977].

[14 AO] Suppose R is a commutative ring, A is a proper ideal in R, and S is a multiplicative semigroup in R not meeting A. Then there is a prime ideal p in R such that A\subseteq p and p\cap S=\emptyset . Rav [1977] and note 80.
[14 BM] A system of equations over a finite ring R has a solution in R if and only if every finite sub-system has a solution in R. Abian [1972] and note 30.
[14 BO] A system of equations over a finite structure (A,\,+,\,\cdot ) has a solution in A, if and only if every finite sub-system has a solution in A. note 30.

226. Let R be a commutative ring with identity, B a proper subring containing 1 and q a prime ideal in B. Then there is a subring A of R and a prime ideal p in A such that (a) B\subseteq A (b) q=B\cap p (c) R-p is multiplicatively closed and (d) if A\neq R, then R-A is multiplicatively closed. Rav [1977].
243. Every principal ideal domain is a unique factorization domain. Hodges [1976a] and note 84.
244. Every principal ideal domain has a maximal ideal. Hodges [1976a] and note 84.
278. In an integral domain R, if every ideal is finitely generated then R has a maximal proper ideal. Hodges [1974] and note 45 E.

[\boldsymbol{0} U] For any class of similar (universal) algebras K,\,HSP\,K=Mod\,Eq\,K. (The class of homomorphic images of subalgebras of products of non-empty families of algebras in K is the same as the class of algebras which satisfy the set of equations holding in every algebra in K.) Andreka/Nemeti [1981] and note 50.

[\boldsymbol{0} V] For every class K of similar algebras SP\,K\supseteq PS\,K. (For any class K of similar algebras, S\,K is the class of all subalgebras of elements of K (not closed under isomorphism) and P\,K is the class of algebras isomorphic to direct products of algebras in K). Andreka/Nemeti [1980].

[\boldsymbol{0} W] For every class K of similar algebras SP^{r}K\supseteq P^{r}S\,K. (For any class K of similar algebras, S\,K is the class of all subalgebras of elements of K (not closed under isomorphism) and P^{r}K is the class of all algebras isomorphic to reduced direct products of algebras in K.) Andreka/Nemeti [1980].

[1 AD] For every class K of similar algebras SP^{g}K\supseteq P^{g}S\,K. (For any class K of similar algebras, S\,K is the class of all subalgebras of elements of K (not closed under isomorphism) and P^{g}K is the class of direct products of elements of K not closed under isomorphism). Andreka/Nemeti [1980].
[1 AP] For any type \tau of the form \tau =(M), every homomorphism of an algebra of type \tau is closed. Diener [1989] and note 115.

[1 AQ] For any type \tau of the form \tau =(M), every homomorphism of an algebra \mathbf{A} of type \tau into an algebra \mathbf{B} of type \tau maps \mathbf{A} onto a subalgebra of \mathbf{B}. Diener [1989] and note 105.

[1 AR] Let S be any family of disjoint non-empty sets and let \tau =(\bigcup S), then any homomorphism from \mathfrak{P}(\tau ;\bigcup \,S) into \mathfrak{P}(\tau ;S) maps \mathfrak{P}(\tau ;\bigcup \,S) onto a subalgebra of :\mathfrak{P}(\tau ;S). Diener [1989] and note 115.
[1 AX] Birkhoff Representation Theorem: Every algebra is isomorphic to a subdirect product of subdirectly irreducible algebras. Birkhoff [1944], Grätzer [1979] and [1986].
[1 BE] Every unique factorization domain can be mapped homomorphically onto a non-zero subdirectly irreducible ring. Rav [1988], Grätzer [1979] pp 122-124 and note 84.

[14 AS] Let \mathfrak{A} and \mathfrak{B} be (universal) algebras of type r where \mathfrak{A} and \mathfrak{B} have underlying sets A and B respectively and B is finite. Suppose for every finite C\subseteq A there is a partial r homomorphism from \mathfrak{A} into \mathfrak{B} with domain C. Then there is an r homomorphism from \mathfrak{A} into \mathfrak{B} . van Benthem [1975].

[43 N] RM1,\,\aleph _{0}: The representation theorem for multi-algebras with \aleph _{0} unary operations: Assume (A,\,F) is a multi-algebra with \aleph _{0} unary operations (and no other operations), then there is an algebra (B,\,G) with \aleph _{0} unary operations and an equivalence relation E on B such that (B/E,\,G/E) and (A,\,F) are isomorphic multi-algebras. Note 50 and Höft/Howard [1981].

[43 O] (Depends on n\in \omega ,\,n\geq 1)\,RM1,\,n: The representation theorem for multi-algebras with n unary operations: Assume (A,\,F) is a multi-algebra with n unary operations (and no other operations), then there is an algebra (B,\,G) with n unary operations and an equivalence relation E on B such that (B/E,\,G/E) and (A,\,F) are isomorphic multi-algebras. Höft/Howard [1981] and note 50.

[67 E] For any algebra \mathbf{A} with finitary operations (that is, \mathbf{A} is of type \tau where \tau =(K_{i})_{i\in I} with K_{i} finite for each i\in I) and for any generating subset Z of \mathbf{A}, there is a function h:A\rightarrow \mathcal{P}_{\omega }(Z) (A is the domain of \mathbf{A} and \mathcal{P}_{\omega }(Z) is the set of all finite subsets of Z.) such that \forall a\in A,\,a is in the subalgebra of \mathbf{A} generated by h(a). Diener [1989] and note 115.

[67 F] For any algebra \mathbf{A} with one unary operation f and any generating set Z of \mathbf{A}, there is a function h:A\rightarrow \mathcal{P}_{\omega }(Z) (A is the domain of \mathbf{A} and \mathcal{P}_{\omega }(Z) is the set of all finite subsets of Z.) such that \forall a\in A,\,a is in the subalgebra of \mathbf{A} generated by h(a). Diener [1989] and note 115.

[88 C] If m is a cardinal number and \mathcal{L} is a lattice isomorphic to the lattice of subalgebras of some unary universal algebra (a unary universal algebra is one with only unary or nullary operations) and \alpha is an automorphism of \mathcal{L} of order 2 (that is, \alpha ^{2} is the identity) then there is a unary algebra \mathfrak{A} with |\,\mathrm{domain}\,(\mathfrak{A})|\geq m and an isomorphism \rho from \mathcal{L} onto the lattice of subalgebras of \mathfrak{A}^{2} with \rho (\alpha (x))=(\rho (x))^{-1}(=\{(s,\,t):(t,\, s)\in \rho (x)\}) for all x\in \mathcal{L}. Lampe [1974].

[88 D] For any cardinal m, there is a unary algebra \mathfrak{A} =\langle A,\, F\rangle (only unary and nullary operations) and a proper subalgebra \mathfrak{D} of \mathfrak{A}^{2} such that \mathfrak{A}^{2} has exactly four subalgebras, \mathfrak{A},\,\emptyset ,\,\mathfrak{D} and \mathfrak{D}^{\ast }=\{(s,\,t):(t,\,s)\in \mathfrak{D}\}. Lampe [1974].
[159 A] Every variety has an initial algebra. Blass [1983b] and note 32.
[159 B] For every variety V and set X,\,V has a free algebra on X. Blass [1983b] and note 32.

174(\alpha ). RM1,\,\aleph _{\alpha }: The representation theorem for multi-algebras with \aleph _{\alpha } unary operations: Assume (A,\,F) is a multi-algebra with \aleph _{\alpha } unary operations (and no other operations). Then there is an algebra (B,\,G) with \aleph _{\alpha } unary operations and an equivalence relation E on B such that (B/E,\,G/E) and (A,\, F) are isomorphic multi-algebras. Höft/Howard [1981] and note 50.

268. If \mathcal{L} is a lattice isomorphic to the lattice of subalgebras of some unary universal algebra (a unary universal algebra is one with only unary or nullary operations) and \alpha is an automorphism of \mathcal{L} of order 2 (that is, \alpha ^{2} is the identity), then there is a unary algebra \mathfrak{A} and an isomorphism \rho from \mathcal{L} onto the lattice of subalgebras of \mathfrak{A}^{2} with \rho (\alpha (x))=(\rho (x))^{-1}(=\{(s,\,t):(t,\,s)\in \rho (x)\}) for all x\in \mathcal{L}. Lampe [1974].

[\boldsymbol{0} AM] Assume V is a separable vector space, D is a countable dense subset of V, and p:V\rightarrow \mathbb{R} satisfies p(x+y)\leq p(x)+p(y), and (\forall t\geq 0)(\forall x\in V)(p(tx)=tp(x)). Also assume that p satisfies the following condition:

Moreover, if f is a linear function from a subspace S of V into \mathbb{R} which satisfies (\forall x\in S)(f(x)\leq p(x)), then f can be extended to f^{\ast }:V\rightarrow \mathbb{R} so that f^{\ast } is linear and (\forall x\in V)(f^{\ast }(x)\leq p(x)). Note 143.
[1 A] In every vector space, every generating set contains a basis. Halpern [1966].
[1 BJ] In every vector space over the two element field, every generating set contains a basis. Keremedis [1996a].
[1 BU] In every vector space over \mathbb{Q}, every generating set includes a basis. Blass [1984a] and note 137.

[1 BZ] Vector Space Multiple Choice: For every family V=\{V_{i}:i\in K\} of non-trivial vector spaces there is a family F=\{F_{i}:i\in K\} such that for each i\in K,\,F_{i} is a non-empty, finite, independent subset of V_{i}. Note 127.

[14 AU] If Z is a real vector lattice with order unit 1 then the set of all positive linear functionals u on Z with u(1)=1 is a convex set that has an extreme point. See H. Rubin/J. Rubin [1985], pages 177 and 182 for definitions. Also see Gardiner [1974].
[43 V] Every convex-compact set in a Hausdorff topological vector space with a basis of convex open sets is Baire. Fossy/Morillon [1995] and note 23.

52. Hahn-Banach Theorem: If V is a real vector space and p:V\rightarrow \mathbb{R} satisfies p(x+y)\leq p(x)+p(y) and (\forall t>0)(p(tx)=tp(x)) and S is a subspace of V and f:S\rightarrow \mathbb{R} is linear and satisfies (\forall x\in S)(f(x)\leq p(x)) then f can be extended to f^{\ast }:V\rightarrow \mathbb{R} such that f^{\ast } is linear and (\forall x\in V)(f^{\ast }(x)\leq p(x)). Lós/Ryll-Nardzewski [1951].
[52 F] If X is a topological vector space then for every continuous sublinear functional p on E there is a linear functional f on E such that f\leq p. Fossy/Morillon [1995].
[52 G] If X is a normed vector space then for every continuous sublinear functional p on E there is alinear functional f on E such that f\leq p. Fossy/Morillon [1995].
[52 H] Existence of Real Valued Banach Limits: For any directed set (\Delta ,\,\sqsubseteq ) there exists a (real valued) Banach limit. Schechter [1996b] and note 31.

[52 I] Real Valued Convex Domination Theorem: For every real vector space X, every subspace X_{0}\subseteq X, every linear \lambda _{0}:X_{0}\rightarrow \mathbb{R} and every convex p:X\rightarrow \mathbb{R}, if \lambda _{0}\leq p on X_{0} then \lambda _{0} can be extended to a linear map \lambda :X\rightarrow \mathbb{R} such that \lambda \leq p on X. Schechter [1996b] and note 31.

[52 J] Support Theorem for Real Valued Convex Functions: For every real vector space X, every convex function p:X\rightarrow \mathbb{R} is a pointwise maximum of affine functions. Schechter [1996b] and note 31.

[52 K] Sandwich Theorem for Real Valued Functions: For every real vector space X, if e:X\rightarrow \mathbb{R} is a concave function, g:X\rightarrow \mathbb{R} is a convex function, and e\leq g everywhere on X, then there exists an affine function f:X\rightarrow \mathbb{R} satisfying e\leq f\leq g everywhere on X. Schechter [1996b] and note 31.

65. The Krein-Milman Theorem: Let K be a compact convex set in a locally convex topological vector space X. Then K has an extreme point. (An extreme point is a point which is not an interior point of any line segment which lies in K.) Royden [1963] and H. Rubin/J. Rubin [1985], p. 177.
66. Every vector space over a field has a basis. Hamel [1905].

95 (F). Existence of Complementary Subspaces over a Field F: If F is a field, then every vector space V over F has the property that if S\subseteq V is a subspace of V, then there is a subspace S^{\prime }\subseteq V such that S\cap S^{\prime }=\{0\} and SUS^{\prime } generates V. Bleicher [1964], [1965], H. Rubin/J. Rubin [1985], pp 119ff, and Jech [1973b], p 148 prob 10.4.
96. Löwig’s Theorem. If B_{1} and B_{2} are both bases for the vector space V then |B_{1}|=|B_{2}|. Löwig [1934].

109. Every field F and every vector space V over F has the property that each linearly independent set A\subseteq V can be extended to a basis. Bleicher [1964], [1965], Blass [1984a], H. Rubin/J. Rubin [1985], pp 119ff.
110. Every vector space over \mathbb{Q} has a basis. Blass [1984a].
195. Every general linear system has a linear global reaction. Note 62 and Harazisville (see Kharazishvili [1979]).

[218 A] Existence of Complementary Subspaces: For every field F, every vector space V over F has the property that if S\subseteq V is a subspace of V, then there is a subspace S^{\prime }\subseteq V such that S\cap S^{\prime }=\{0\} and SUS^{\prime } generates V. Bleicher [1964], [1965], H. Rubin/J. Rubin [1985], pp 123ff, Theorems 6.36, 6.37, and 6.38.
235. If V is a vector space and B_{1} and B_{2} are bases for V then |B_{1}| and |B_{2}| are comparable. Gross [1976].
236. If V is a vector space with a basis and S is a linearly independent subset of V such that no proper extension of S is a basis for V, then S is a basis for V. Gross [1975], [1976].
[236 A] If V is a vector space with a basis, then every linearly independent subset is contained in a basis.

286. Extended Krein-Milman Theorem: Let \mathrm{K} be a quasicompact (sometimes called convex-compact), convex subset of a locally convex topological vector space, then \mathrm{K} has an extreme point. H. Rubin/J. Rubin [1985], p. 177–178 and note 23.

287. The Hahn-Banach Theorem for Separable Normed Linear Spaces: Assume V is a separable normed linear space and p:V\rightarrow \mathbb{R} satisfies p(x+y)\leq p(x)+ p(y) and (\forall t\geq 0)(\forall x\in V)(p(tx)=tp(x)) and assume f is a linear function from a subspace S of V into \mathbb{R} which satisfies (\forall x\in S)(f(x)\leq p(x)), then f can be extended to f^{\ast }:V\rightarrow \mathbb{R} so that f^{\ast } is linear and (\forall x\in V)(f^{\ast }(x)\leq p(x)). Note 145.
[333 A] In every vector space B over the two element field, every subspace of B has a complementary subspace. Keremedis [1996a].

346. Vector Space Kinna-Wagner Principle: For every family V=\{V_{i}:i\in K\} of non-trivial vector spaces there is a family F=\{F_{i}:i\in K\} such that for each i\in K,\,F_{i} is a non-empty, independent subset of V_{i}. Note 127.
367. There is a Hamel basis for \mathbb{R} as a vector space over \mathbb{Q}. Hamel [1905].

372. Generalized Hahn-Banach Theorem: Assume that X is a real vector space, (Z,\preccurlyeq ) is a Dedekind complete ordered vector space and X_{0} is a subspace of X. If \lambda _{0}:X_{0}\rightarrow Z is linear and p:X\rightarrow Z is sublinear and if \lambda _{0}\preccurlyeq p on X_{0} then \lambda _{0} can be extended to a linear map \lambda :X\rightarrow Z such that \lambda \preccurlyeq p on X. Schechter [1996b] and note 31.

[372 A] Existence of Banach Limits: For any directed set (\triangle ,\,\sqsubseteq ) and any Dedekind complete ordered vector space (Z,\preccurlyeq ) there exists a Z-valued Banach limit. Schechter [1996b] and note 31.

[372 B] Generalized Convex Domination Theorem: For every real vector space X, every Dedekind complete ordered vector space (Z,\preccurlyeq ), every subspace X_{0}\subseteq X, every linear \lambda _{0}:X_{0}\rightarrow Z and every convex p:X\rightarrow Z, if \lambda _{0}\preccurlyeq p on X_{0} then \lambda _{0} can be extended to a linear map \lambda :X\rightarrow Z such that \lambda \preccurlyeq p on X. Schechter [1996b] and note 31.

[372 C] Generalized Support Theorem: For every real vector space X and every Dedekind complete ordered vector space (Z,\preccurlyeq ), every convex function p:X\rightarrow Z is a pointwise maximum of affine functions. Schechter [1996b] and note 31.

[372 D] Generalized Sandwich Theorem: For every real vector space X and every Dedekind complete ordered vector space (Z,\,\preccurlyeq ), if e:X\rightarrow Z is a concave function, g:X\rightarrow Z is a convex function, and e\leq g everywhere on X, then there exists an affine function f:X\rightarrow Z satisfying e\leq f\leq g everywhere on X. Schechter [1996b] and note 31.

sec.title: ANALYSIS (FORMS FROM ANALYSIS)
sec.p: [\boldsymbol{0} H] F. Riesz Theorem: A Hilbert space is finite dimensional iff its closed unit ball is compact. Brunner [1983b].
[\boldsymbol{0} I] The following are equivalent in a Hilbert space:

def.p: The closed unit ball is sequentially compact.
Each unconditionally convergent series converges absolutely.
Each ortho-normal system is Dedekind finite.

sec.p: Brunner [1983b] and note 94.

[\boldsymbol{0} AM] Assume V is a separable vector space, D is a countable dense subset of V, and p:V\rightarrow \mathbb{R} satisfies p(x+y)\leq p(x)+p(y), and (\forall t\geq 0)(\forall x\in V)(p(tx)=tp(x)). Also assume that p satisfies the following condition:

Moreover, if f is a linear function from a subspace S of V into \mathbb{R} which satisfies (\forall x\in S)(f(x)\leq p(x)), then f can be extended to f^{\ast }:V\rightarrow \mathbb{R} so that f^{\ast } is linear and (\forall x\in V)(f^{\ast }(x)\leq p(x)). Note 143.
[8 E] In a metric space every sequentially continuous real valued function is continuous. Brunner [1982c].
[10 D] In every Hilbert space with a Dedekind finite orthonormal basis, the closed unit ball is sequentially compact. Brunner [1983b] and note 94.
[14 Q] Alaoglu’s Theorem: The unit ball is compact in the weak^{\ast } topology in the dual of a Banach space. (See [52 E].) Johnstone [1984] and note 23.
[14 U] Every closed proper ideal in a Gelfand algebra is contained in some maximal ideal. Banaschewski [1983] and note 29.
[14 BY] For every topological space X, every proper ideal in the normed \mathbb{R}-algebra of continuous bounded functions from X into \mathbb{R} is contained in a maximal ideal. Morillon [1988].
[14 BZ] Every proper ideal in a non-trivial normed \mathbb{R}-algebra or \mathbb{C}-algebra with identity is contained in a maximal ideal. Morillon [1988].

[14 CA] If (A_{i})_{i\in I} is a family of non trivial commutative normed algebras with identity then there is a family (J_{i})_{i\in I} such that for each i\in I,\,J_{i} is a maximal ideal in A_{i}. Morillon [1988].

[14 CB] If X is a topological space and I is a proper ideal in the algebra of all bounded continuous functions from X to \mathbb{R} such that every function in I vanishes at at least one point of X then I is contained in a maximal ideal. Morillon [1988].
[14 CL] Gelfand Extreme Point Theorem: If A is a non-trivial Gelfand algebra then the closed unit ball in the dual of A has an extreme point e with e\neq 0. Morillon [1986], notes 23 and 29.
[52 E] The unit ball is convex-compact in the weak^{\ast } topology in the dual of a Banach space. (See [14 Q].) Luxemburg [1969], H. Rubin /J. Rubin [1985] p 178, and note 23.

65. The Krein-Milman Theorem: Let K be a compact convex set in a locally convex topological vector space X. Then K has an extreme point. (An extreme point is a point which is not an interior point of any line segment which lies in K.) Royden [1963] and H. Rubin/J. Rubin [1985], p. 177.

[118 V] If (L,\,\leq ) is a linear order and G=\{[l_{i},\,r_{i}]:i\in K\} is a locally finite family of closed intervals of L whose interiors are non-empty and pairwise disjoint, then there exists a continuous real valued function f:L\rightarrow \mathbb{R} such that |f^{-1}(0)\cap [l_{i},\,r_{i}]|\geq 2 and |f^{-1}(1) \cap [l_{i},\,r_{i}]|\geq 1 for all i\in K. Keremedis [1995] and note 43.

[118 W] If (L,\,\leq ) is a linear order and G=\{[l_{i},\,r_{i}]:i\in K\} is a locally finite family of closed intervals of L whose interiors are non-empty and pairwise disjoint, then there exists a continuous real valued function f:L\rightarrow \mathbb{R} such that for each i\in K,\,f(l_{i})=f(r_{i})=0 and f(x)>0 for all x\in (l_{i},\,r_{i}). Keremedis [1995] and note 43.

[118 X] If (L,\,\leq ) is a complete linear order and G=\{(l_{i},\,r_{i}):i\in K\} is a family of open, non-empty, pairwise disjoint intervals of L, then there exists a set \{f_{i}:i\in K\} of non constant continuous real valued functions on L such that for each i\in K,\,f_{i} vanishes outside of (l_{i},\, r_{i}). Keremedis [1995].

124. Every operator on a Hilbert space with an amorphous base is the direct sum of a finite matrix and a scalar operator. (A set is amorphous if it is not the union of two disjoint infinite sets.) Brunner [1984a].
[126 A] Every positive functional on a B-lattice is continuous. Brunner [1984d] and note 16.
153. The closed unit ball of a Hilbert space is compact in the weak topology. Fossy/Morillon [1995] and Rudin [1991].
156. Theorem of Gelfand and Kolmogoroff: Two compact T_{2} spaces are homeomorphic if their rings of real valued continuous functions are isomorphic. Brunner [1983a] and Gelfand/Kolmogoroff [1939].

157. Theorem of Goodner: A compact T_{2} space is extremally disconnected (the closure of every open set is open) if and only if each non-empty subset of C(X) (set of continuous real valued functions on X) which is pointwise bounded has a supremum. Goodner [1950].
158. In every Hilbert space H, if the closed unit ball is sequentially compact, then H has an orthonormal basis. Brunner [1983b].

279. The Closed Graph Theorem for operations between Fréchet Spaces: Suppose X and Y are Fréchet spaces, T:X\rightarrow Y is linear and G=\{(x,\,Tx): x\in X\} is closed in X\times Y. Then T is continuous. Rudin [1991] p. 51, Wright [1973], note 96.
281. There is a Hilbert space H and an unbounded linear operator on H. Wright [1973], note 96.

286. Extended Krein-Milman Theorem: Let \mathrm{K} be a quasicompact (sometimes called convex-compact), convex subset of a locally convex topological vector space, then \mathrm{K} has an extreme point. H. Rubin/J. Rubin [1985], p. 177–178 and note 23.

287. The Hahn-Banach Theorem for Separable Normed Linear Spaces: Assume V is a separable normed linear space and p:V\rightarrow \mathbb{R} satisfies p(x+y)\leq p(x)+ p(y) and (\forall t\geq 0)(\forall x\in V)(p(tx)=tp(x)) and assume f is a linear function from a subspace S of V into \mathbb{R} which satisfies (\forall x\in S)(f(x)\leq p(x)), then f can be extended to f^{\ast }:V\rightarrow \mathbb{R} so that f^{\ast } is linear and (\forall x\in V)(f^{\ast }(x)\leq p(x)). Note 145.
370. Weak Gelfand Extreme Point Theorem: If A is a non-trivial Gelfand algebra then the closed unit ball in the dual of A has an extreme point e. Morillon [1986], notes 23 and 29.

sec.title: CARDINAL NUMBER FORMS
sec.p: [\boldsymbol{0} AL] For every set A, there is an \aleph which cannot be covered by fewer than |A| sets each of cardinality <|A|. Note 131.
25. \aleph _{\beta +1} is regular for all ordinals \beta . Feferman/Levy [1963] and Gitik [1980].
34. \aleph _{1} is regular. Russell [1906] and note 3.

[40 B] For all ordinals \alpha , the \aleph _{\alpha } partition principle holds: For every ordinal \alpha and every cardinal \kappa , if \aleph _{\alpha }\leq ^{\ast }\kappa , then \aleph _{\alpha }\leq \kappa . Pelc [1978], Banaschewski/Moore [1990], and note 69.
41. W_{\aleph _{1}}: For every cardinal m,\,m\leq \aleph _{1} or \aleph _{1}\leq m. Jech [1973b].
54. For all infinite cardinals m,\,m adj 2^{m} implies m is an aleph. (m\ adj\ n iff m<n and (\neg \exists p)(m<p<n).) Mathias [1979] prob 1337, thm 1338 and prob 1339.
56. \aleph (2^{\aleph _{0}})\neq \aleph _{\omega }. (\aleph (2^{\aleph _{0}}) is Hartogs’ aleph, the least \aleph not \leq 2^{\aleph _{0}}.) Mathias [1979] p 125.

58. There is an ordinal \alpha such that \aleph (2^{\aleph _{\alpha }})\neq \aleph _{\alpha +1}. (\aleph (2^{\aleph _{\alpha }}) is Hartogs’ aleph, the least \aleph not \leq 2^{\aleph _{\alpha }}.) Mathias [1979] p 126.
71(\alpha ). W_{\aleph _{\alpha }}:(\forall x)(|x|\leq \aleph _{\alpha } or |x|\geq \aleph _{\alpha }). Pelc [1978], Jech [1973b], page 119 and Levy [1964].
104. There is a regular uncountable aleph. Jech [1966b] p 165 prob 11.26.
108. There is an ordinal \alpha such that 2^{\aleph _{\alpha }} is not the union of a denumerable set of denumerable sets. Gitik [1985].
159. The regular cardinals are cofinal in the class of ordinals. Blass [1983b].
170. \aleph _{1}\leq 2^{\aleph _{0}}. Bernstein [1908] and Banaschewski/Moore [1990].
182. There is an aleph whose cofinality is greater than \aleph _{0}. Gitik [1980].
183(\alpha ). There are no \aleph _{\alpha } minimal sets. That is, there are no sets X such that

def.p: |X| is incomparable with \aleph _{\alpha }
\aleph _{\beta }<|X| for every \beta <\alpha and
\forall Y\subseteq X,\,|Y|<\aleph _{\alpha } or |X-Y|<\aleph _{\alpha }.

sec.p: Hickman [1980b] and note 56.
208. For all ordinals \alpha ,\,\aleph _{\alpha +1}\leq 2^{\aleph _{\alpha }}. Figura [1977].
209. There is an ordinal \alpha such that for all X, if X is a denumerable union of denumerable sets then \mathcal{P}(X) cannot be partitioned into \aleph _{\alpha } non-empty sets. Morris [1970].
245. There is a function f:\omega _{1}\rightarrow \omega _{1}^{\omega } such that for every \alpha ,\, 0<\alpha <\omega _{1},\,f(\alpha ) is a function from \omega onto \alpha . Litman [1976].

[245 A] There is a function g:\omega _{1}\rightarrow \omega _{1}^{\omega } such that for all limit ordinals \alpha <\omega _{1},\,g(\alpha ) is an increasing function from \omega into \alpha with the range of g cofinal in \alpha . Litman [1976]

[245 B] Every closed set A in \omega _{1} which contains only limit ordinals is a derivative (that is, \exists B\subseteq \omega _{1} such that A=\{x:x\ {is a limit and}\ \{t:t\in B\}\ {is cofinal in}\ x\}.) Litman [1976].
246. The monadic theory theory MT(\omega _{1},\,<) of \omega _{1} is recursive. Litman [1976] and note 85.
275. The sequence of cardinals \langle \aleph _{n}: n\in \omega \rangle has a unique minimal upper bound. Truss [1974b].

315. \Omega =\omega _{1}, where \Omega =\{\alpha \in \ \mathrm{On}: (\forall \beta \leq \alpha )(\beta =0\vee (\exists \gamma )(\beta =\gamma + 1) \vee there is a sequence \langle \gamma _{n}: n\in \omega \rangle such that for each n\ \gamma _{n}<\beta and \beta =\bigcup \nolimits _{n<\omega }\gamma _{n}\} Gitik [1980].
365. For every uncountable set A, if A has the same cardinality as each of its uncountable subsets then |A|=\aleph _{1}. Sierpiński [1918].
[\boldsymbol{0} A] Cardinal successors 2: For every cardinal m there is a cardinal n such that m<n and (\neg \exists p)(m<p<n). Tarski [1954a] and Jech [1966a].

[\boldsymbol{0} F] Cancellation for surjective cardinal equivalence: For every k\in w-\{0\},\,(\forall x\forall y)(kx=^{\ast } ky\ \mathrm{implies}\ x=^{\ast } y) (The expression x=^{\ast }y means that there is a function f from x onto y and a function g from y onto x.) Truss [1984].

[\boldsymbol{0} G] Cancellation for injective cardinal inequality: For every k\in \omega -\{0\},\,(\forall x\forall y)(kx\leq ky\ \mathrm{implies}\ x\leq y) (\leq is the usual (injective) cardinal ordering.) Lindenbaum/Tarski [1926].
[\boldsymbol{0} Q] For all cardinal numbers m and n and Dedekind finite cardinals p, if p+m=p+n then m=n. Tarski [1949b] and note 94
[1 D] Cardinal successors 3: For every cardinal m there is a cardinal n such that m<n and (\forall p)(m<p\rightarrow n\leq p). Tarski [1954a] and Jech [1966a].
2. Existence of successor cardinals: For every cardinal m there is a cardinal n such that m<n and (\forall p<n)(p\leq m). Tarski [1954a].
3. 2m=m: For all infinite cardinals m,\,2m=m. Tarski [1954a].
[3 A] For all cardinals m and n,\,n\leq m and m infinite \rightarrow m+n=m. Halpern/Howard [1970].
[3 B] \aleph _{0}\cdot m=m: For all infinite cardinals m,\,\aleph _{0}\cdot m=m. Halpern/Howard [1970].

[3 C] Definability of cardinal addition as the least upper bound: (For all cardinals x,\,y and z) (x+y=z iff (x\leq z and y\leq z and (\forall u)(x,\,y\leq u\rightarrow z\leq u)). Häussler [1983] and Tarski [1949a].

[9 F] There is no subset A of the class of Dedekind finite cardinals such that A under the usual cardinal ordering is order isomorphic to \langle \mathbb{R}, \leq \rangle . Tarski [1965], Jech [1973b] p 161 prob 6, and note 94.
[9 K] If A is uncountable and B is countable, then |A-B|=|A|. G. Moore [1982] p 201.
[9 L] If A is uncountable and B is countable, then |A\cup B|=|A|. G. Moore [1982] p 202.
[9 M] If \aleph _{0}<|A| and \aleph _{0}=|B|, then \aleph _{0}<|A-B|. G. Moore [1982] p 202.
[9 N] If \aleph _{0}\leq ^{\ast }m, then \aleph _{0}\leq m. Lindenbaum/Tarski [1926], G. Moore [1982] p 216, and note 69.
[9 O] m\leq \aleph _{0} or \aleph _{0}\leq m. Lindenbaum/Tarski [1926] and G. Moore [1982] p 216,
[9 P] If m+\aleph _{0}<n +\aleph _{0}, then m<n. Lindenbaum/Tarski [1926] and G. Moore [1982] p 216.
[9 Q] If m+\aleph _{0}=n+\aleph _{0}, then m=n or m,\,n\leq \aleph _{0}. Lindenbaum/Tarski [1926] and G. Moore [1982] p 216.
53. For all infinite cardinals m,\,m^{2}\leq 2^{m}. Mathias [1979] prob 1336.
55. For all infinite cardinals m and n, if m\cdot n=m+n then, m\leq n or n\leq m. Mathias [1979] p 125.
136(k). Surjective Cardinal Cancellation (depends on k\in \omega -\{0\}): For all cardinals x and y,\,kx\leq ^{\ast }ky implies x\leq ^{\ast }y. Truss [1984] and note 69.
161. Definability of cardinal addition in terms of \leq : There is a first order formula whose only non-logical symbol is \leq (for cardinals) that defines cardinal addition. Häussler [1983].
162. Non-existence of infinite units: There is no infinite cardinal number A such that A+A>A and for all cardinals x and y,\,x+y=A\rightarrow x=A or y=A. Häussler [1983].
200. For all infinite x,\,|2^{x}|=|x!|. Dawson/Howard [1976] and note 64.
204. For every infinite X, there is a function from X onto 2X. Truss [1978].
277. E(D,\,VII): Every non-well-orderable cardinal is decomposable. Monro [1973a] and note 94.
283. Cardinality of well ordered subsets: For all n\in \omega and for all infinite x,\,|x^{n}|<|s(x)| where s(x) is the set of all well orderable subsets of x. Truss [1973d].
290. For all infinite x,\,|2^{x}|=|x^{x}|. Pincus [1978] and note 64.
